### Skool Agent — Banned-Phrase Hardening After 2026-05-11 Moderation Strike (2026-05-12)
- [x] Diagnosed: 2026-05-11 Skool moderation flag on `skool_responses.id = 1c21a93f-6271-4ebf-8018-e3c264381dde` ("Congrats on the positive feedback, Harsh! ... DM me if you want to dig into this. - Ali Muwwakkil"). Response was generated 2026-05-03 (5 days BEFORE the 2026-05-08 OpenClaw banned-phrase fix), passed the Skool quality gate with score=100, then posted 2026-05-11. Critically, this is a **DIFFERENT subsystem** from OpenClaw — Skool has its own agent tree under `backend/src/services/agents/skool/` with its own quality gate, its own response table, and its own prompt strategy. The 2026-05-08 OpenClaw patch did not touch this code path at all.
- [x] `backend/src/services/agents/skool/skoolPlatformStrategy.ts` — three fixes: (1) Rewrote the `direct` (hiring-category) CTA instruction. The OLD prompt **explicitly told the LLM** to use `"DM me if you want to dig into this"` or `"Happy to share more in a DM if useful"` as soft CTAs — those were Skool moderation flag triggers verbatim. NEW instruction bans every flavor of DM-bait and instructs the model to "Close with VALUE, not invitation." Also flags the recurring "multi-agent voice system for a logistics client" framing as a fingerprint. (2) Added an `ABSOLUTE BANS` rule #11 to the top-level RESPONSE RULES section listing every flagged pattern explicitly, applied universally across all categories. (3) Extended `validateContent()` (the LLM-output gate at generation time) with a `dmBaitPatterns` array that rejects any reply containing DM me / message me / dig into this / happy to chat-share-discuss-connect-help-assist / feel free to reach out / contact me directly / if you're looking to partner / if you're interested / let me know if you want — regardless of category.
  - Date: 2026-05-12
  - Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 in backend
- [x] `backend/src/services/agents/skool/skoolQualityGateAgent.ts` — added a `universalDmBaitPatterns` check BEFORE the existing `!isHiringCategory` branch. Previous structure put all DM-bait patterns inside the non-hiring branch, so `category='hiring'` responses bypassed them entirely (that's why the 2026-05-11 flagged comment scored 100). New patterns also include `\bif you'?re (looking to|interested in) (partner|collaborat|work with me|connect)/i`, `\bif you'?re interested\s*[.,!]/i`, `\blet me know if you (want|need|are interested|'?d like)/i`, `\bhappy to share (more )?about\b/i`. Also moved the canned `\bmulti[- ]agent voice system\b` case-study fingerprint check into the non-hiring branch.
  - Date: 2026-05-12
  - Verification: tsc clean
- [x] **Retroactive cleanup**: ran `UPDATE skool_responses SET post_status='failed', quality_score=50, metadata=...` for any row currently `post_status='approved' AND posted_at IS NULL` whose body matched the new banned-phrase regex set. **41 of 311 pending Skool posts contained at least one banned phrase** and were re-flagged before they could post. Each carries `metadata.retro_rejection_reason = 'Contains DM-bait / share-CTA pattern flagged on 2026-05-11 Skool moderation strike. Auto-rejected during 2026-05-12 retroactive sweep.'` for audit. Sample IDs: `7ed66882-…`, `88e06d0b-…`, `ee3c81ad-…`, `f4866701-…`, `ba7ea372-…` (full 41-row list returned by RETURNING clause).
  - Date: 2026-05-12
  - Verification: `UPDATE 41` returned by Postgres
  - Notes: this addresses the **immediate posting risk** (these 41 would have shipped to Skool over the next 1-2 days and likely triggered cascading moderation strikes). The code fixes above prevent future ones from being approved.

### Inbox Agent — Hard Rule Tuning to Stop Auto-Notification Leakage (2026-05-12)
- [x] `backend/src/services/inbox/hardRuleEngine.ts` — fixed two over-firing hard rules that were leaking ~129 emails over 3 days into the user-facing inbox. (1) **Name check** restricted to subject only (was scanning body too) AND now skipped entirely for known auto-notification domains via `AUTO_NOTIFICATION_SENDERS` regex (basecamp.com, rocketmortgage.com, zoom.us, dart.org, opentable.com, substack.com, lyftmail.com, nextdoor.com, otter.ai, mailchimp.com, sendgrid.net, amazonses.com). Basecamp injects "Ali Muwwakkil" into the body of every project notification (assignment lists, recipient lists, @-mentions) so the old `namePattern.test(body)` was treating every Basecamp email as "directly addressed to Ali". (2) **Priority-keyword check** dropped 'school' from the list (`daycare, sports league, parent teacher, pta, field trip` remain). Ali runs Colaberry's data school so every internal school-related email was tripping a kid-school keyword filter.
  - Date: 2026-05-12
  - What changed: hardRuleEngine name check now `!isAutoNotificationSender && namePattern.test(email.subject)`; 'school' removed from `priorityKeywords`.
  - Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0 in backend; root cause was confirmed via 3 prod SQL queries — last 3 days had 107 INBOX-state classifications via "Directly addressed to Ali Muwwakkil" reason (75 of which were Basecamp notifications that the table-driven Basecamp rule should have routed to AUTOMATION but never got the chance because hard rules run first) and 22 INBOX via "Contains priority keyword: school" reason.
  - Notes: deferred deploy per "production deploys only after hours" rule. DB rule additions (below) take effect immediately on the next classification. Code change ships on next prod deploy.
- [x] Added 3 rows to `inbox_rules` table in prod for senders that had no rule at all: Rocket Mortgage receipts (id `309f6dba-0c4e-4f2f-9f7e-41cc47e15d60`), DART notifications (id `a790bcad-dd4d-4ecc-813a-212bb313b2c1`), OpenTable confirmations (id `88bdd973-ef43-4d98-a762-ee6d0dd25410`). All `target_state=AUTOMATION`, `priority=20`, `enabled=true`, condition `from CONTAINS <domain>`.
  - Date: 2026-05-12
  - Verification: `INSERT 0 3` returned by Postgres; rules visible via `SELECT * FROM inbox_rules WHERE created_by = 'inbox-audit-2026-05-12'`
  - Notes: priority 20 > priority 10 (existing Basecamp rule) so these win during user-defined-rule iteration. But they still run AFTER hard rules — so the code fix above is the load-bearing change; these DB rules are belt-and-suspenders coverage.

Replaces "stress-test → confirm → giant phase" loop with HTML→critique→prompt→rebuild loop. Pivot mandate: backend cognition substrate (Phases 1–32, 1,732 tests) is mature; bottleneck has moved to product clarity, operational simplicity, execution confidence, visual trust, onboarding, guided product creation UX. Five priorities sequenced for fastest perceived value: P1 Visual Engineering Workspace (`frontend/src/features/visualWorkspace/` — embed + pin + group + compile prompt; the marquee feature; ~3–5 days), P2 Unified Cory Home (replace ProjectDashboard landing; ~2–3 days), P3 Build Center (one execution lane, deep-link from everywhere; ~2–4 days), P4 Verification Workspace (last-24h check feed + manifest auto-rerun; ~2–3 days), P5 UnifiedProjectState (one backend synthesizer + one frontend hook + lint rule against local recompute; ~4–6 days, ships in parallel). Hard non-goals: NO Phase 33; NO new cognition subsystems; NO new chat agent / mentor agent / orchestration layer; NO co-pilot panels competing with Cory. Existing governance (Phases 1–32) stays — it just stops owning UI surface and becomes background intelligence (drawer, not foreground).

- [x] Analysis: requirements-generator comparison (Architect vs regular LLM)
  - Date: 2026-05-21
  - What changed: Ran a controlled head-to-head on the same idea (ShelfSense). Architect: 253-char idea → 13,742 words / 108,442 chars (~23 pages, 7 chapters), 429× explosion. Regular (gpt-4o-mini, 1 call, max_tokens 16,000): 1,068-char prompt → 1,450 words / 10,580 chars (~2 pages), and only 24% of the requested 6,000 words. Architect is 10.2× the size. Key findings: single-call LLM self-limits well below its token cap; the Architect's chunked per-chapter generation (≥1,750 words/chapter, retried) is what reaches depth; the Architect ignores the questionnaire (built from idea only) while the regular path is the only one that uses it.
  - Verification: report `docs/REQUIREMENTS_GENERATOR_COMPARISON.html`; raw `docs/doc-comparison/{metrics.json,architect.md,regular.md}`.
  - Notes: Recommendations — basic workflow: regular path (tailored/fast/cheap) but add a 2-pass section-expand to fix the length shortfall; full system: Architect; and feed the questionnaire INTO the Architect so its 23 pages match what the user actually selected.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/compareDocGenerators.js` + `scripts/buildDocComparisonReport.js` + `docs/REQUIREMENTS_GENERATOR_COMPARISON.html` | New: controlled doc-generator comparison (fetches Architect doc + generates a regular-LLM doc for the same idea, job-only/not saved) + report generator + report (2026-05-21) |

- [x] Fix: activateProject no longer marks a 0-capability build-out as activated
  - Date: 2026-05-21
  - What changed: `activateProject()` clustered requirements in a swallowed try/catch and then unconditionally set `activated=true` — so when clustering failed/returned nothing (observed on run3's ~100KB Architect doc) the user got a "ready" project with 0 capabilities after a ~15-min wait. Now: clustering retries once if it yields 0 capabilities, and if it's still 0 the function throws (project left un-activated) instead of marking it complete. Callers (`POST /setup/activate`, `architect-status`) record the failure and can retry.
  - Verification: backend `tsc --noEmit` passes; deployed to prod; functional activate confirmed still produces capabilities + activates normally.
  - Notes: The retry alone fixes the observed transient run3 case (a manual re-trigger had populated it); the throw is the safety net so an empty build-out is never presented as success.

|---|---|

- [x] Fix: requirements generation could hang for ~30 min (unbounded OpenAI call)
  - Date: 2026-05-21
  - What changed: A Workflow generation job hung in `running` (doc length 0) for 15+ min during timing tests — the OpenAI SDK default is a 10-min timeout with 2 retries (~30 min worst case), and the 2-pass expand doubles the exposure. `getOpenAI()` now sets `timeout: 240000, maxRetries: 1`, so a stalled call fails the job cleanly (the UI surfaces a retry) instead of spinning. Frontend generation poll budget raised 10→15 min to accommodate the legitimate 2-pass duration; Workflow chooser estimate updated ~3→~5 min.
  - Verification: backend + frontend `tsc --noEmit` pass; production build compiles; deployed; Workflow re-run completes (timing run).
  - Notes: Failure-First compliance — the external LLM call is now bounded. Surfaced while documenting the 3 paths with a richer idea (more capabilities → larger prompt → exposed the unbounded-call hang).

|---|---|
| `backend/src/services/requirementsGenerationService.ts` | `getOpenAI()` sets `timeout: 240000, maxRetries: 1` so generation calls can't hang indefinitely (2026-05-21) |

- [x] Three operator-flagged issues from Lead Ingestion BP detail review (BPs tab + Components tab on portal)
  - Date: 2026-05-22
  - What changed: Operator opened the Lead Ingestion BP modal on `/portal/project/system?tab=bps&layer=backend` and reported three things: (1) the "Learn about this BP" chip strip + per-step "Ask Cory" links were INVISIBLE even though the operator was `ali@colaberry.com`, contradicting the prior session's review HTML; (2) the walkthrough cards suggested "Generate the backend prompt" for a backend already marked "In place (forming)" — button verb said GENERATE while the copy said EXTEND, plus steps never went away when the layer was fully done; (3) the BPs tab and Components tab displayed the same B/F/A layer state with different visual vocabularies — gray vs red for missing, icons vs text badges. Three commits, executed in order (`b0b13c7c`, `57881bf4`, `c25321d0`):
    1. **`b0b13c7c` — Cory portal gate fallback.** Root cause of (1): the `useCoryAvailable` hook only consulted `useAdminUser`, which reads `admin_token` and hits `/api/admin/me`. On `/portal/*` routes the operator authenticates via `participant_token`; if `admin_token` is missing or expired, the gate returns `false` even for authorized identities. Fix: `useCoryAvailable` now also decodes the `participant_token` JWT claims client-side (base64url payload, no signature verification — server still enforces auth on every API call) and accepts the same identity predicate (`email==ali@colaberry.com OR role==super_admin`) from either token source. Caveat documented in the hook's doc-block: the actual Cory chat (`coryApi.ts`) still calls `/api/admin/intelligence/cory` with `admin_token`, so a portal-only operator with no `admin_token` will see the chip strip render but the chat call will 401 — that's a separate auth-scope question, not this commit's scope.
    2. **`57881bf4` — Walkthrough state-aware labels + step suppression.** Audited `bpStepWalkthrough.ts`: `ctaLabel` was a static string ("Generate X prompt") regardless of layer state, while `whatItDoes` + `whyItMatters` correctly switched to "extend" language when the layer was partial. Mixed signal. Steps also never suppressed when a layer was fully present (only the agent step had a suppression rule, and only at confirmedAgents≥3 + matLevel≥4). Now: `ctaLabel` is "Generate X prompt" for missing, "Extend X prompt" for partial. Step suppressed entirely when `usability === 'ready'/'present' AND unmatched requirements === 0`. Page-kind caps still always render their upgrade step (a page is always improvable). Backend `/prompt` endpoint dispatch unchanged — the `step.key` enum is preserved so this is purely UI prose + suppression.
    3. **`c25321d0` — Visual parity across BPs and Components tabs.** Reversed the 2026-05-20 intentional divergence ("BPs asks 'what's present?', Components asks 'is it wired?'") in favor of operator mental-model consistency. `bpSignals.ts` `PILLAR_TONES.missing` collapsed from red (#b91c1c) to gray (#9ca3af) — both tabs now use the same palette. Extracted `BuiltnessIcon` + `deriveBuiltnessProps(bp)` helper into a new shared file `BPBuiltnessIcon.tsx`. `BPDomainSurfaceRows.tsx` dropped its local `PILLAR_TONES` shadow + the no-op `.map()` that re-applied it; `CapabilityGrid.tsx` dropped its inline "Built / Wired / Partial / Not built yet" text badge in favor of the shared icon. Card left-border tonal accent in CapabilityGrid still uses `bpBuiltness` for color choice — unchanged. Trade-off: loses the "red = needs work" cue in Components tab; gains one vocabulary across both surfaces.
  - Verification: frontend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; CRA production build (`CI=true npm run build`) exit 0; deployed to VPS below; production `HTTP 200` confirmed below.

The review HTML should be updated to reflect the corrected behavior. Pre-existing jest infra issue on `bpSignals.test.ts` (babel parser doesn't recognize the `type` keyword in import statements) blocked unit-test verification of the palette change; not caused by this work — flagged separately. `tsc --noEmit` + production CRA build are the operative verification gates.

- [x] SECURITY FIX + Plan A Phase 1: Cory routes gated; portal Cory chat unblocked (`29d22a75`)
  - Date: 2026-05-22
  - What changed: Pre-existing security defect surfaced during plan reconnaissance: `backend/src/routes/admin/coryRoutes.ts` (committed in `593a5530` when Cory was first added) had ZERO authentication middleware on its 19 endpoints — `/command`, `/hire-agent`, `/retire-agent`, `/agent-proposals/:id/approve`, `/evolution/run`, etc. were callable by any unauthenticated request that knew the URL. Every other admin route (`leadRoutes.ts`, `campaignRoutes.ts`, etc.) applies `requireAdmin` per-route; coryRoutes had been missed at first-author time and never caught. Operator was notified before any change; explicit go-ahead recorded for the merged scope (close the security hole AND add the portal-unblock at the same time, since the implementation is identical code with a different framing). New `requireCoryAuthorized` middleware in `authMiddleware.ts` (alongside `requireAdmin`, not replacing it): accepts `admin_token` OR `participant_token`, verifies JWT, gates on the Cory-specific identity predicate (`email === 'ali@colaberry.com'` OR `role === 'super_admin'`) — same predicate the frontend's `useCoryAvailable()` already uses, so client and server agree symmetrically. On success populates `req.admin` (same shape as `requireAdmin`) so downstream Cory handlers work unchanged. Applied via `router.use(requireCoryAuthorized)` at the top of `coryRoutes.ts` — covers all 19 endpoints uniformly. Frontend `coryApi.ts` interceptor now sends `admin_token` if present, falls back to `participant_token` — unblocks Cory chat on portal (which authenticates via `participant_token` only; the prior interceptor sent nothing on portal so even the `useCoryAvailable` gate passing didn't help — chat call would 401 anyway).
  - Verification: backend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; frontend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; CRA production build (`CI=true npm run build`) exit 0; deployed (backend + nginx rebuilt); production probes confirm gate live: `GET /api/admin/intelligence/cory/status` (no auth) returns 401 (was 200 before); `POST /command` (no auth) returns 401; garbage token returns 401; landing page still HTTP 200 in ~400 ms. Brief 502 window (~60-90s) during backend container boot — expected behavior on every backend deploy, not caused by this change.
  - Notes: Plan A Phase 1 of the Cory unified-surface plan, executed with revised framing per the security finding. The original framing was "relax existing auth to accept participant_token"; the reality was "add first-time auth designed to accept both tokens from authorized identities." Same code, different outcome — closes a real security hole AND unblocks portal Cory in one commit. Behavioral consequences explicitly enumerated in the commit message: Ali's existing admin flow unchanged; Ali on portal newly works; anonymous calls newly blocked; other admins (without `super_admin` role) lose access they shouldn't have had (codebase audit confirms nobody is in this bucket today). Next: Plan A Phases 2-5 (deprecate standalone Cory page links → conversation persistence → tiered project context per operator's instinct to mirror Claude Code's approach → entry-point expansion) per the plan HTML in `docs/CORY_UNIFIED_AND_BLUEPRINT_REPORT_PLAN.html`.

| `backend/src/routes/admin/coryRoutes.ts` | Imports `requireCoryAuthorized`; applies via `router.use(...)` at the top — gates all 19 Cory endpoints uniformly. (2026-05-22) |

Root cause was in another session's commit `29d22a75` (Cory routes auth gate): `coryRoutes.ts` mounted `requireCoryAuthorized` as a router-wide middleware (`router.use(requireCoryAuthorized)`), and because `coryRoutes` is mounted in `adminRoutes` without a path prefix, **every request that reached that sub-router was gated** — including non-Cory requests passing through `adminRoutes` (mounted first in server.ts) on their way to `participantRoutes`/`projectRoutes`. Fix is one line: path-scope the gate to the actual Cory prefix (`router.use('/api/admin/intelligence/cory', requireCoryAuthorized)`). Security intent preserved (all 19 cory endpoints still gated, they all share that prefix); no other request flow gets blocked.

  - Notes: Cross-instance fix — `coryRoutes.ts` was authored by session `CC-...` (commit 29d22a75, "Cory routes auth gate"). Per CLAUDE.md's Concurrent-instance safety rules I normally don't edit another instance's code, but the regression had bricked portal participants. Surgical, security-preserving change with the rationale logged in code comments so the originating session can see it.

- [x] HOT FIX: agentOrphanRoutes path-scoped — portal was returning 401 on every request since 2026-05-26 deploy
  - Date: 2026-05-27
  - Session: CC-20260527-7g2k
  - What changed: While building a Plan C video walkthrough I noticed `curl https://enterprise.colaberry.ai/api/portal/verify?token=...` was returning 401 — an endpoint that is intentionally unauthenticated. Root cause: my `backend/src/routes/admin/agentOrphanRoutes.ts` from 2026-05-26 (commit `1e622e40`) used `router.use(requireAdmin)` ROUTER-WIDE instead of path-scoping it. Because that sub-router is mounted in `adminRoutes` without a path prefix, and `adminRoutes` is mounted first in `server.ts`, **every request flowing through the admin router was getting `requireAdmin`-gated before reaching `participantRoutes` / `projectRoutes`** — including the unauthenticated `/api/portal/verify` magic-link endpoint. Portal users were getting 401 on every request since the 2026-05-26 deploy. This is the EXACT same regression pattern as commit `c209d49e` (the Cory router-wide gate from 2026-05-26 earlier this morning) — I should have learned from it and didn't. Fix is one line: `router.use('/api/admin/agent-orphans', requireAdmin)` instead of `router.use(requireAdmin)`. Identified before any user complaint via the smoke probe but the portal was broken for ~24 hours.
  - Verification: backend `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; production smoke probes after deploy — `GET /api/portal/verify?token=…` returns `200` (was 401); `GET /api/portal/profile` returns `401` unauthed (was 401, unchanged); `GET /api/admin/agent-orphans?projectId=…` still returns `401` unauthed (gate still live for the admin surface). Plan C video walkthrough below worked end-to-end after the fix.
  - Notes: This is a process failure on my part — the Cory regression got fixed earlier this exact session and documented in detail in PROGRESS.md and in the commit message of `c209d49e`. I built `agentOrphanRoutes.ts` the same day and replicated the exact same mistake. Lesson, stamped here: **when adding `router.use(middleware)` in any sub-router mounted in `adminRoutes`, the middleware MUST be path-scoped to the actual route prefix.** Should add a lint rule or codebase comment somewhere prominent. The mental model "router.use applies only inside this file" is wrong — it applies to every request that PASSES THROUGH the router on its way to other routers below it.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `backend/src/routes/admin/agentOrphanRoutes.ts` | `router.use(requireAdmin)` → `router.use('/api/admin/agent-orphans', requireAdmin)`. Inline comment documents the regression pattern + connects it to the prior c209d49e Cory fix for future readers. (2026-05-27) |

- [x] **Inbox spam-leak fix: archiveGmail() now honors Gmail rate-limit Retry-After + catch-up sweep clears stuck queue.**
  - Date: 2026-06-09
  - Session: CC-20260609-a3k7
  - What changed: Audit triggered by Ali seeing newsletter/promo spam (julian@ffit40.com, bylt, tripadvisor, googlealerts, etc.) in his Outlook inbox. Root cause: `backend/src/services/inbox/autoArchiveService.ts` `archiveGmail()` was issuing a single Gmail `messages.modify` call with no retry. When Gmail returned 403/429 with `userRateLimitExceeded` (which it had during a 67-call burst on 2026-06-07 16:42 UTC), the call threw, the wrapping `archiveEmail()` logged `archive_failed` to `inbox_audit_logs`, and the email stayed with the `INBOX` label on Gmail — visible in Outlook forever even though classified `AUTOMATION` in the DB. 69 stuck emails in the last 48h (12% archive failure rate on `gmail_colaberry`). **Fix**: added `parseGmailRetryAfterMs(error)` that recognizes Gmail rate-limit signals from both 429 status and 403+`rateLimitExceeded` reason; parses the wait hint from the `Retry-After` header OR from the `Retry after <ISO>` token embedded in Gmail's error message; defaults to 2s when classified as rate-limit but no parseable hint. New retry loop in `archiveGmail()` runs up to 3 attempts with each wait capped at 30s. Non-rate-limit errors still throw immediately on first attempt — preserves the existing dead-letter path. `archiveHotmail()` unchanged (Graph had 0 failures in the 48h window).
  - Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` from `/backend` exited 0. Deployed to prod VPS (during business hours, explicit Ali override of after-hours rule — spam was actively in inbox). At the top of `sendWithBcAttach()` (before Mandrill), `resolveBcToken()` calls `getBasecampToken()` which is CCPP-preferred when `MSSQL_HOST` is set, ignoring whatever stale `BASECAMP_ACCESS_TOKEN` dotenv loaded from the VPS `.env`. **(2) BC preflight.** Before the Mandrill send, the helper does a raw `fetch` against `GET /buckets/{bucketId}/recordings/{ticketId}.json` and checks status-only (no `r.json()` — BC returns 204 No Content for many todo types and bcGet's unconditional JSON parse would crash even on a valid recording). On non-2xx, throw with the clear message "sendWithBcAttach BC preflight failed (Mandrill send aborted)" + the failing path + the BC response body (first 200 chars). Guarantees: if Mandrill ships, the BC attach will almost certainly ship too; and if it doesn't, a retry is safe because the preflight will fail again the same way. Docstring at the top of the helper updated to document both behaviors.

Total Mandrill calls across both runs: 0. The 404 (not 401) on BC also confirms the token resolution path is using a live valid token from CCPP. Caught a real bug between the two commits — first attempt at the preflight used the existing `bcGet` helper, which crashed on 204 No Content (the recording WAS accessible, but `r.json()` failed on empty body); fixed in the second commit by switching to a raw fetch + status-only check + body drain for socket cleanup. Syntax check (`node -c`) passed on both commits.
  - Notes: **Behaviour change for callers**: if anyone was implicitly depending on the prior behavior of skipping a real BC verification (e.g., posting against a ticketId that doesn't exist and tolerating the late failure), they'll now fail fast at preflight instead. That's the desired contract per the doctrine. **What's still not handled**: transient BC failure AFTER the preflight passed but BEFORE the comment post — Mandrill could ship and BC could blink. The retry would re-send Mandrill. Mitigation: in practice this requires BC failing in the ~100ms window between preflight and comment post, which is rare; the fix-vs-effort tradeoff didn't justify the per-call state file approach. If it happens, the reconciliation pattern from today (post the comment manually with a doctrine-compliance note) still works. **Follow-ups not done**: (1) delete the stale BASECAMP_ACCESS_TOKEN from `/opt/colaberry-accelerator/.env` so future scripts that read it directly without going through getBasecampToken hit a clean "not set" error instead of a stale value; (2) add a CI/preflight check that all outbound-email scripts use `sendWithBcAttach` rather than raw nodemailer (since the helper is now the only path that gets the live token without footguns). - [x] **Inbox spam-leak P3: restored gmail_personal sync via OAuth re-consent + client pivot (broken GCP client `596...` → working `241...`).**
  - Date: 2026-06-10
  - Session: CC-20260609-a3k7
  - What changed: Personal Gmail (`alimuwwakkil@gmail.com`) had been silently dark for an unknown period — every sync cycle was failing with `invalid_grant` from Google's token endpoint, so no classification, archiving, or VIP routing was happening on that account. Root cause turned out to be deeper than expected token expiry. **Step 1 — OAuth re-consent**: Ran `scripts/inbox-auth-helper.js` locally; first attempt blocked by the GCP project's OAuth consent screen (`LandJet Growth Engine`, Error 403 `org_internal`) because Chrome auto-selected `ali@colaberry.com` session instead of using the personal-account login_hint. Re-ran in Incognito → flow completed against the `241...` (workspace) client because local `.env` was missing `GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_ID` and fell back to `GMAIL_CLIENT_ID` per the helper's `||` chain. **Step 2 — root cause discovery**: After updating prod's `GMAIL_PERSONAL_REFRESH_TOKEN` to the freshly-issued value, sync started failing with `unauthorized_client` / `Unauthorized` from Google's token endpoint. Direct `curl POST oauth2.googleapis.com/token` from inside the prod container reproduced the error. Diagnosed by trying the same refresh token with the alternate `GMAIL_CLIENT_ID` (`241...`) credentials — that combo returned a valid `access_token`, proving the token was issued by `241...`, not by the prod-configured `GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_ID` (`596...`). The `596...` client appears to have had its secret rotated or been deleted in GCP (Google rejects refresh-token grant despite accepting auth-code grant from local — but that auth-code grant had actually used the `241...` fallback, not `596...`). **Step 3 — fix**: Pointed prod's `GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_ID` and `GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_SECRET` to the same values as `GMAIL_CLIENT_ID` / `GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET` (the working `241...` client). Force-recreated `accelerator-backend` so the new env values landed in the container. Sync immediately succeeded — `[gmail_personal] Found 49 messages to sync` → `Synced 49 messages, 49 new`. **Files touched**: prod `/opt/colaberry-accelerator/.env` only — no code changes. Backed up as `.env.bak.<timestamp>` on each rotation step. Also rolled back local `.env` to remove the leaked `GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_ID`/`GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_SECRET` that I had copied in from prod's broken-client values during diagnosis (those would mislead future helper runs).
  - Verification: `docker compose ... exec backend curl -X POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token -d grant_type=refresh_token -d refresh_token=$GMAIL_PERSONAL_REFRESH_TOKEN -d client_id=$GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_ID -d client_secret=$GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_SECRET` now returns `{access_token, expires_in:3599, ...}`. Live log: `[InboxCOS][Sync] [gmail_personal] Found 49 messages to sync` followed by `Synced 49 messages, 49 new`. Hotmail also audited as part of the question "could this have been the same problem with hotmail?" — confirmed healthy: 102 emails synced in last 7 days, latest 2026-06-10 06:23 UTC; `[InboxCOS][Graph] Refresh token rotated — update MS_GRAPH_REFRESH_TOKEN env var` warning is cosmetic only because the Graph client is configured with a client_secret (confidential client), so Microsoft allows indefinite refresh-token reuse even though it rotates the token in the response.
  - Notes: **Long-term cleanup**: prod now uses the same OAuth client (`241...`) for both `gmail_colaberry` and `gmail_personal`. Functionally equivalent, but if anyone ever wants to revoke one without affecting the other, a dedicated personal-account OAuth client should be re-created in a Colaberry-owned GCP project (set External from the start, add `alimuwwakkil@gmail.com` as test user, copy new client_id/secret into prod's `GMAIL_PERSONAL_*` env vars). The `596...` client should be either repaired or deleted in GCP. **Local-machine cleanup performed**: removed the broken `GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_ID=596...` / `GMAIL_PERSONAL_CLIENT_SECRET=...` lines I added to local `.env` during diagnosis — local now has only `GMAIL_CLIENT_ID`/`GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET` so the helper falls back to those correctly. **Hotmail `Refresh token rotated` warning**: worth eventually silencing in `msGraphService.ts` so the warning doesn't lead future-me down a false rabbit hole — Microsoft's confidential-client refresh tokens don't actually need rotation persistence. Not done this session; logged for follow-up.

- [x] **ops priorityEngine — dedup on urgency_score only (stops category ping-pong with automation).**
  - Date: 2026-06-15
  - Session: CC-20260615-r7m2
  - What changed: After dedup+retention+guard, prod `ops_ai_assessments` still grew ~40k rows/cron-cycle. Root cause found: `ops_bc_todos.category` is co-owned. The priority engine sets it, then `automationRulesService` (runs after the engine in the same 2-min cron: sync→score→automation) overwrites it via `UPDATE ops_bc_todos SET category = :tagval` (e.g. to `waiting_dependency`). The next engine pass saw category flipped, treated the todo as "changed", wrote an audit row + overwrote category back — an infinite ping-pong producing one audit row per todo per cycle even though `urgency_score` never moved (verified in prod: a written todo had 6 writes / 1 distinct score, and stored category=`waiting_dependency` while the engine's audit rows said `human_required`). Fix in `backend/src/services/ops/priorityEngineService.ts`: replaced `assessmentChanged` (score+category) with `scoreChanged` (urgency_score only). `urgency_score` is owned solely by the engine (automation never writes it), so it is the stable, authoritative dedup key. Score-stable todos now skip both the UPDATE and the audit insert, which also stops the engine from re-fighting automation over category. Removed the now-unused `prev_category` SELECT column + field.
  - Verification: `scoreChanged` unit test rewritten (null/equal/changed/string-normalize/NaN). Source type-clean (no external importers of the old helper; worktree tsc errors were junction-only dependency-resolution artifacts). Authoritative check post-deploy: prod steady-state audit-row growth over N cron cycles with no manual passes (see deploy measurement).
  - Notes: This is the fix that actually bounds the table. The category co-ownership between priorityEngine and automationRulesService is a real latent design issue (which service should own `category`?) worth a deliberate owner decision, but excluding category from the engine's dedup resolves the disk-growth symptom without changing automation behavior.

Pure decision logic extracted and exported behind a `require.main === module` guard.
  - Verification: `npx jest src/scripts/__tests__/govContractsTurnWatcher.test.ts` -> 19/19 pass, including defect-guard cases (already-fired handoff does not re-emit; N completions -> one turn; re-detecting a fired completion yields zero turns; failed-send bid left un-advanced for retry; no em-dashes survive rendering). `node --check` passes. Deployed to prod host: cherry-picked onto `main`, pushed, `git pull` on the VPS host checkout (the watcher is a root cron, every 5 min, not container code), then re-baselined the state file so the fix takes effect on the next tick.

- [x] **fix: UXRemediationOutcome over-long index name broke sync({ alter: true }) on every boot.**
  - Date: 2026-06-16
  - Session: CC-20260615-r7m2
  - What changed: The composite index `['project_id','cluster_signature','observed_at']` on `ux_remediation_outcomes` had no explicit name, so Sequelize generated `ux_remediation_outcomes_project_id_cluster_signature_observed_at` (64 chars). Postgres truncates identifiers to 63, so the on-disk index is `..._observed_a`. Sequelize then searched for the full 64-char name on every `sequelize.sync({ alter: true })` (run at backend boot), never found it, tried to re-CREATE it, and failed with "relation ... already exists" — aborting schema auto-migration each boot (seen in prod logs after the GitHub-integration deploy; same root cause as the dev1 seedAdmin failure). Pinned the index `name` to the existing 63-char identifier in `backend/src/models/UXRemediationOutcome.ts`. Sibling `RemediationOutcome` checked — single-column indexes only, no risk.
  - Verification: zero DB migration (name matches the index already on disk in prod/dev1/dev2 and is <=63 so fresh DBs create it cleanly). Post-deploy: prod backend boot logs no longer show the `sync({ alter: true }) failed ... already exists` error. tsc unaffected (config-only change).
  - Notes: Non-fatal before the fix (app booted; the catch swallowed it) but it silently disabled schema auto-migration — any future model change would not auto-apply. This unblocks that. Identifier-length is a latent trap for any new long composite index; keep generated names <=63 or set an explicit short name.

- [x] **cb-system-handler — cut the "forced-reply" quality defect at the source (retry on tool_choice:'required' before force-wrapping prose).**
  - Date: 2026-06-17
  - Session: CC-20260617-w2p8
  - What changed: The daily `cb-quality-audit.js` flagged 12/25 @CB responses (~48%) as the "forced-reply (model returned text without a real tool_call)" defect. Root cause in `scripts/ops-engine/cb-system-handler.js`: the agent loop ran every turn with `tool_choice: 'auto'`, and whenever the model answered in plain prose instead of calling `basecamp_reply`, the handler went straight to the force-wrap branch (`calls.length === 0`) — bypassing the proper tool path, which is what the audit counts as a defect. Fix: on the first tool-less turn, escalate `tool_choice` to `'required'` and retry once (gated by `toolChoiceRetryUsed` so it can't loop), pushing a system nudge to call `basecamp_reply`; the model's prose is preserved in `messages` so the retry refines rather than discards it. Only if the single retry is also tool-less does it fall back to the existing force-wrap (which still runs `looksLikeToolCallLeak` + sanitizer), so the requester always gets an answer. `tool_choice` then stays `'required'` for the rest of the invocation, enforcing the "end with basecamp_reply, then finish" protocol.
  - Verification: `node --check scripts/ops-engine/cb-system-handler.js` passes. Self-verifying in production — `cb-quality-audit.js --learn` (daily 12:15 UTC cron) measures the forced-reply rate, so a drop in the defect count on tomorrow's audit confirms the fix. Pre-fix corrective check: ran `cb-self-improve.js --days 5` (DRY) on the VPS first — 0 reposts / 423 skipped, confirming the already-posted forced replies were substantively fine (no live cleanup owed), so this is purely a forward-looking source fix.
  - Notes: Committed directly to `main` from an isolated worktree (`hotfix/cb-forced-reply-fix` off `origin/main`), NOT via the `workstream/interview-prep-report` branch — that branch has diverged from main and is MISSING the current CB system (`cb-quality-audit.js`, `cb-self-improve.js`, `cb-reply-sanitizer.js`, `cb-replay.js`) plus the dispatcher hardening; merging it would delete that system from prod. The fix was re-applied against main's actual 1056-line handler (the branch copy was 130 lines stale). Host-cron operational script (not container code) — took effect on the next dispatcher tick after the VPS `git pull origin main`, no docker rebuild. **Lesson from #70 testing — GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN is NOT a prod env var:**
The manual test seeded `github_connections.access_token_encrypted` directly with a personal access token. Production never uses a global `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN` — each student's OAuth token is stored per-row in `github_connections` after they connect via the OAuth flow (`/api/portal/github/oauth/callback`). Ali does not need to add `GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN` to the prod server. The existing env vars (`GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_URL`, `GITHUB_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI`) are sufficient. The cron job is a no-op until at least one student completes the OAuth flow and has a repo connected.

- [x] **P0 fix: support@ classification crashed on `rule_id` UUID type — Cora never ran in prod**
  - Date: 2026-06-18
  - Session: CC-20260618-c7r4
  - What changed: End-to-end trace of support@ → Cora (after deploying the out-of-scope routing fix) surfaced a production-down bug, live since PR #30 merged (2026-06-17): `inbox_classifications.rule_id` is a Postgres **UUID** column, but `hardRuleEngine` writes the string `rule_id: 'cora_0c'`. The classification `INSERT` in `inboxStateManager` Step 3 threw `invalid input syntax for type uuid: "cora_0c"` **before** dispatch, so `handleCoraInquiry` was never called — every support@ email failed classification, was never archived, and was re-selected every 60s poll (the pipeline only picks up rows with no classification), stuck in an infinite failed-retry loop. Cora had **never** processed a real support@ email in prod; the thread's "shadow test" used the standalone `testCoraEmail.ts` (direct `generateCoraReply`, no DB insert), which bypassed the failing path.
    - `backend/src/services/inbox/ruleIdPersistence.ts` (new): pure `isUuid()` + `toPersistableRuleId()` — persist a rule_id only when it is a real UUID, else null.
    - `backend/src/services/inbox/inboxStateManager.ts`: Step 3 insert now uses `rule_id: toPersistableRuleId(ruleId)`. The in-memory `ruleId` still drives `dispatchByState` (so `cora_0c` dispatch works) and `reasoning` records the matched rule, so no information is lost. `cora_0c` was the only offending string id (the other rule_id at hardRuleEngine:263 uses a real UUID).
  - Verification: `tsc --noEmit` clean (backend, exit 0). New unit suite `backend/src/services/inbox/__tests__/ruleIdPersistence.test.ts` — 8 tests (UUID accept incl. uppercase; reject `cora_0c`/empty/null/undefined/non-string; malformed-UUID boundary; UUID passthrough; idempotency). Post-deploy: the ~4 stuck support@ emails self-heal on the next poll (still unclassified, so reprocessed cleanly).
  - Notes: Chosen fix is code-only (Ali's call) — no schema change, no migration, reversible, lowest blast radius. **Follow-up (tracked):** widen `inbox_classifications.rule_id` to `VARCHAR` so it can store semantic rule names properly; then the sanitize guard becomes belt-and-suspenders. Branch `workstream/cora-ruleid-persist` off `origin/main` (post-#42) in an isolated worktree. This is what actually makes Cora — and the #42 out-of-scope routing — functional.

- [x] **Trace coverage fix: never-null trace_id on every LLM call (TBI P1-4)**
  - Date: 2026-06-23
  - Session: CC-20260622-r468
  - What changed: Backlog-loop iteration. A live query found **916 of 977 `openai/llm.call` events (7d) were untraced** (`trace_id=null`) → traceCoveragePct stuck at **12%**. Root cause: the instrumented OpenAI wrapper resolved `trace_id` as `context.trace_id ?? getTraceId() ?? null`, so the 4 background entry points that call the LLM outside any request/cron context (`ai_message` 564, `inbox_classify` 206, `assistant` 118, `inbox_reply` 28) emitted null. Fix: new `requestContext.ensureTraceId(explicit?)` = `explicit → current context → fresh uuid` (never null), applied once per call in `openaiInstrumented` (replacing the three `?? getTraceId() ?? null` sites). No-ops when a context already exists (HTTP/cron paths unchanged); background callers now get a per-call correlatable id instead of null. Lifts the Observability **`trace`** criterion (live) from open(12) toward met as new events accumulate.
  - Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx jest requestContext` 4/4 (explicit wins / context id / fresh-uuid-when-absent). Post-deploy: confirmed new `llm.call` events carry `trace_id` (recent-window coverage jumps from 12%).
  - Notes: Found by querying the data, not guessing — an Explore agent had wrongly claimed `instrumentCronJob` doesn't wrap `fn()` in a context; reading the code showed it DOES (scheduler crons already traced), so the real gap was contextless background service calls. Per-call seeding gives coverage + single-call correlation; true per-job correlation for multi-call agentic background flows is a later entry-level-context improvement. traceCoveragePct is a rolling 7d metric, so the dashboard climbs to ~full over the next few days as untraced events age out.

  - Date: 2026-06-25
  - Session: CC-20260623-e2k7
  - What changed: Found the send queue clogged with phantom work: 456 of 458 "due" email actions had already been emailed (matching outbound communication_log) but their row never flipped pending->sent (process restarted between send and status-update, incl. mid-window deploys), leaving them stuck at attempts_made >= max_attempts where the fetch (`attempts_made < max_attempts`) skips them forever. Idempotent, ~0 rows steady-state, non-blocking. Unclogs the fetch + makes metrics honest + prevents recurrence.
  - Verification: post-deploy, the 458-stuck backlog clears on the first cycle (stuck-due count -> ~0, fetchable count rises); AI ROI Pilot Touch-2 shows 99 sent.
  - Notes: Subject-matched comm-log is the proof-of-send (each touch has a unique subject per lead) so re-sending is avoided. Lesson reinforced: deploy after-hours; mid-window restarts strand in-flight sends (this reconciler now self-corrects that within one cycle).

- [x] **PR #110 remediation: kill the content_hash collision between catalog scraper and content watcher**
  - Date: 2026-06-30
  - Session: CC-20260630-rp10
  - What changed:
    - `backend/src/services/anthropicContentWatcher.ts` — `runContentWatcher()` now queries `findAll({ where: { content_type: { [Op.ne]: 'course' } } })` (added `import { Op } from 'sequelize'`). Course rows are owned exclusively by `anthropicCatalogScraper`, which hashes the course OUTLINE into `content_hash`; the watcher hashes the FULL page body into the same column. Without this filter the two services overwrote each other's hash on every run and perpetually flipped `change_detected=true`, firing false curriculum-change alerts to Ali via `anthropicChangeDetector` → `anthropicCurriculumImpactAgent`. This also matches the product intent: course rows alert only on real outline/link changes, not arbitrary page churn.
    - `backend/src/services/anthropicCatalogScraper.ts` — (1) false-alert guard: a fresh scrape that yields an empty outline (failed fetch / selector miss) on an existing course no longer overwrites the stored good outline or flags a change — it bumps `last_checked` only. (2) de-dup `coursesToWatch` by `normalizeCourseUrl` before the sync loop (curriculum_course_links maps many week-rows onto one course, which inflated counts). (3) added `any`-justification comments on the three catch clauses per CLAUDE.md.
    - `backend/src/routes/admin/anthropicRoutes.ts` — corrected the stale comment on the catalog route (it reads tracked URLs from curriculum_course_links, it does not scrape /learn).
    - `backend/src/__tests__/services/anthropicContentWatcher.test.ts` — new test asserting the watcher excludes `content_type='course'` (collision proof).
    - `backend/src/services/__tests__/anthropicCatalogScraper.test.ts` — new tests for the empty-outline false-alert guard and the URL de-dup.
  - Verification: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; Jest 27/27 pass (`anthropicContentWatcher` + `anthropicCatalogScraper` suites, including the 3 new tests). Resolves the major finding from the pr-approval-review verdict on PR #110.
  - Notes: Driven by the remediate-pr loop in an isolated worktree off `origin/workstream/anthropic-catalog-scraper`. Prod still requires `add_outline_to_anthropic_content_registry.sql` applied before deploy (unchanged from the base PR).
  - Follow-up (commit ac704cd5, same session): cleared the remaining false-alert nits from the second pr-approval-review pass — (1) `ORDER BY module_number ASC` on the `curriculum_course_links` read so the first-wins de-dup is deterministic (no Postgres row-order flake flipping a title); (2) a brand-new course created with an empty (failed-scrape) outline is created quietly (`change_detected:false`), not flagged — the next successful scrape flags the real change; (3) `POST /api/admin/sync/anthropic-catalog` catch now carries the `any`-justification comment and returns a generic 500 (stops leaking `err.message`), matching the sibling impact route. Tests updated to assert the quiet empty-create and deterministic ordering. Verification: `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; Jest 27/27; all 4 GitHub CI checks green on both commits. Fresh pr-approval-review verdict: APPROVE_WITH_NITS, 0 blockers, 0 majors.

- [x] **CB System reply: fix the "Aleem Aleem" requester-name doubling (on top of the a7k2 resolver)**
  - Date: 2026-07-01
  - Session: CC-20260701-q8r3
  - What changed: Ali on BC todo 10048624254 - CB's reply doubled the addressee's name ("Aleem Aleem, I've created a task..."). Root cause: prompt rule #6 tells the model to address the requester by PLAIN first name ("Aleem, ..."), then `basecamp_reply` prepended `mention(requesterRef)` (which renders the same name) on top. `injectMentions` only rewrites `@`-prefixed names, so the plain leading name survived and the tag was added beside it.   - Verification: `node --test __tests__/cb-reply-body.test.js` 8/8 (incl. the exact "Aleem Aleem" regression, div-wrapped address, third-party @Sohail no-double, unresolved @Name still tags requester, tool-call-leak wasLeak, mid-sentence not promoted); `node --test __tests__/cb-people.test.js` 20/20 unchanged (no regression); `node --check` clean on cb-reply-body.js / cb-system-handler.js / inbound-dispatcher.js. Repro against the real prod input now renders a single "@Aleem, ..." across all four addressing shapes.
  - Notes: Builds on CC-20260701-a7k2 (same branch/PR #122). The a7k2 resolver is already live on prod, so the doubling is live now - this fix needs an after-hours deploy (host-side `git checkout` of the 3 ops-engine files, CB is a live agent) to actually stop it in prod. - [x] **Fix `backend/Dockerfile` layer-cache ordering — ordinary code changes no longer re-download Playwright/apt/Docker-CLI**
  - Date: 2026-07-07
  - Session: CC-20260706-w2k5
  - Branch: `chore/dockerfile-layer-cache-order`
  - What changed: Reordered the runtime stage of `backend/Dockerfile`. Previously `COPY --from=builder /app/backend/dist` (which changes on every commit) sat *before* the `xvfb`/`git`/`curl`/`gnupg` apt install, the Docker CLI + buildx + compose plugin apt install, and `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` — since Docker's layer cache is linear (one cache miss invalidates every subsequent layer in the stage regardless of that layer's own inputs), every ordinary source-only rebuild was re-running all of that unrelated, multi-minute work. Moved the two apt-install `RUN`s and the Playwright install (plus the `node_modules`/`package.json` copies it depends on, which are themselves cache-stable across source changes since `npm ci` runs before `COPY backend/` in the builder stage) ahead of `COPY --from=builder /app/backend/dist` and the `frontend/src/pages` copy, so only the layers that actually depend on changed source now invalidate on a normal commit.
  - Verification: Rebuilt cold once to confirm the reordered Dockerfile still builds correctly end-to-end (`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml build backend` — full success, image tagged). Then made a trivial source-only edit to `communityService.ts` (reverted after the test) and rebuilt again: build output showed `CACHED` for the `xvfb` apt install, the Docker-CLI apt install, the `node_modules` copy, the `package.json` copy, and the Playwright install — only `COPY --from=builder /app/backend/dist` (3.2s) and the `frontend/src/pages` copy (0.7s) re-ran. Restarted the container from the rebuilt image: boot log shows `Server running on port 3001 [development]`, `restarts=0`; `curl localhost:3012/api/portal/community/posts` (no auth) returned the expected `401`, confirming the container actually serves requests, not just boots.
  - Notes: Pure infra change, no application code touched — kept on its own branch/commit per the "don't bundle a refactor into a feature commit" rule, separate from the two community-feature PRs it was found during. Not deployed to production; the same reorder applies there on the next prod image build, no action needed beyond the normal deploy. Nothing committed yet.

## VA ERP / Gov Contracts — REQ-003 approval gate + fail-closed roles for ERP push (2026-07-13)
- [x] STORY-002 follow-up — human approval-gate on ERP writes (TBI L5) + fail-closed role check
  - Date: 2026-07-13
  - Session: CC-20260713-k3n8
  - What changed: Landed the REQ-003 approval-gate that STORY-002 deferred, and closed the `allowedRoles: []` fail-open hole — the two pre-live follow-ups flagged on PR #191. (1) `backend/src/services/agentAutonomy.ts`: added a HITL rule so high-stakes legacy-ERP writes (action `erp_data_push`, or `resourceType: 'legacy_erp_module'`) always require human approval — reusing the existing ABAC/HITL policy rather than inventing a parallel gate. (2) `backend/src/services/integration/legacyErpIntegrationAgent.ts` (`runLegacyErpPushAgent`): every push now goes through the `authorizeAgentAction` ABAC chokepoint; when governance denies (enforce mode) the write is HELD (`action: erp_data_push_held_for_approval`, `result: flagged`) and no HTTP call fires — "AI proposes, human approves." Shadow-first: in the default shadow mode it records the would-deny exposure and proceeds, so this ships dark and is flipped on at go-live via the `abac_enforcement=enforce` setting. (3) `backend/src/services/integration/legacyErpClient.ts` (`pushUpdate`): role check is now FAIL CLOSED — an empty/absent `allowedRoles` denies (was: open access).
  - Verification: `npx jest agentAutonomy legacyErpUpdateAgent legacyErpIntegrationAgent --runInBand` — 38/38 pass (new: ERP HITL-rule test; runner "held for approval" test; fail-closed "empty allowedRoles denies" test; existing direct-push tests updated to pass an explicit ACL). `tsc --noEmit` over the source changes reported only the unrelated pre-existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` missing-dep in the local worktree — CI backend typecheck is authoritative.
  - Notes: Deliberately integrates with the existing L5 ABAC framework (`agentAutonomy` + `agentAuthorizationService`), NOT a new approval system — the human-facing approval queue / review endpoint / trust dashboard remain the later REQ-003 stories (005/008/009/010/011) + REQ-009 per the Traceability Matrix. Still open (not code): the 6 `VA_ERP_*` env vars are boot-safe (all default; `VA_ERP_MODULE_CONFIG` defaults to `[]` → agent inert) but need real VA OAuth credentials + module endpoints in prod `.env` before any live run — blocked on VA API access, not a build task.

- [x] STORY-003 — real-time data synchronization with legacy ERP modules
  - Date: 2026-07-13
  - Session: CC-20260710-p9k4
  - What changed: New `backend/src/services/integration/realtimeSyncEngine.ts` — `emitPlatformChange(event)` publishes a platform-change event on an in-process `EventEmitter`, standing in for "WebSocket or similar real-time communication protocol": the VA ERP Integration Platform IS this backend, so there's no external client to hold a socket open for; any future caller (a model hook, a route handler) can call `emitPlatformChange()` the moment data changes, satisfying "set up event listeners for changes" with zero added transport/infra. `syncPlatformChange(event, moduleConfigs, maxAttempts?)` is the testable core: routes every sync through the SAME ABAC chokepoint STORY-002's approval-gate uses (`authorizeAgentAction` with `resourceType: 'legacy_erp_module'`) — a real-time trigger doesn't get to bypass the human-approval gate a manual push would hit — then calls `pushUpdate()` (reused from STORY-002) with its own outer retry loop (default 2 attempts, exponential backoff), and writes a dedicated `action: 'erp_realtime_sync'` audit log entry (outcome: success/failure/held, attempt count, duration) distinct from `pushUpdate`'s own `erp_data_push` entry. `startRealtimeSync(moduleConfigs, options)` subscribes to the event bus and returns an unsubscribe function. `backend/src/services/integration/legacyErpIntegrationAgent.ts`: added `startLegacyErpRealtimeSyncAgent()` — thin wrapper matching the other two runners' entry-point pattern, but returns an unsubscribe function instead of an `AgentExecutionResult` since real-time sync is a standing subscription, not a one-shot batch (documented inline). `backend/src/services/integration/types.ts`: added `PlatformChangeEvent`, `RealtimeSyncResult`. New `backend/src/__tests__/services/realtimeSyncEngine.test.ts` — 6 tests: happy path + audit log content, ABAC hold (no fetch fires), retry-then-succeed, retry-exhausted-then-fail (both retry tests account for `pushUpdate`'s compensating-rollback fetch call by having the snapshot fail on failing attempts, avoiding the same mock-misalignment bug fixed in STORY-002's tests), event-bus wiring (emit → sync → unsubscribe stops further syncs), and the agent-runner wrapper.
  - Verification: `npx tsc --noEmit` from `backend/` exits 0. `npx jest legacyErpIntegrationAgent legacyErpUpdateAgent realtimeSyncEngine` — 31/31 pass.
  - Notes: Retry mechanism is a small, fixed outer layer (2 attempts) deliberately independent of `env.vaErpMaxRetries` — compounding it with `pushUpdate`'s own inner HTTP-level retry would let one change trigger a retry storm against a legacy system. Fulfills REQ-001, REQ-004. No Dockerfile change needed (same pattern as STORY-001/002 — `COPY backend/` picks up new files automatically).

## Unsubscribe hardening — one-click (RFC 8058) opt-out endpoint + visible link + scanner watchdog (2026-07-13)

This closes the gap with a real, self-serve, automated opt-out. (1) NEW `backend/src/services/unsubscribeTokenService.ts`: stateless HMAC-SHA256 token binding `leadId`+`email`, domain-separated by a context prefix, `env.unsubscribeSecret` (falls back to the prod-required JWT secret so no new env var is needed to ship); `buildUnsubscribeUrl()` mints `…/api/unsubscribe?lid=&sig=`. (2) NEW `backend/src/controllers/unsubscribeController.ts` + `backend/src/routes/unsubscribeRoutes.ts` (registered in `server.ts` before the JSON parser): `GET /api/unsubscribe` (human link → confirmation page) and `POST /api/unsubscribe` (RFC 8058 one-click; providers POST `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`). Zod-validated, opt-out only fires on a signature matching the lead's current email (id-guessing can't opt anyone out), idempotent (already-unsubscribed short-circuits — no duplicate `UnsubscribeEvent`), 503-not-false-success on DB error. (3) `backend/src/services/schedulerService.ts`: campaign sends now advertise `List-Unsubscribe: <https one-click>, <mailto>` + `List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`, and both `wrapPersonalEmailHtml` (subtle) and `wrapEmailHtml` render a visible signed Unsubscribe link (mailto fallback when no lead id). (4) `backend/src/config/env.ts`: `unsubscribeSecret`, `publicAppUrl` (default `https://enterprise.colaberry.ai`). (5) NEW `scripts/unsubscribe-health-check.js`: external host-cron watchdog that emails Ali (Mandrill) if the Inbox COS scanner goes stale (last `inbox_emails.synced_at` too old) OR any active lead's unsubscribe-subject email is unprocessed — catches the silent single-point-of-failure of the in-process timers.

## Cora auto-reply loop guards + opt-in send default (2026-07-14)
- [x] Stop Cora's self-reply storm at the source: loop guards + default-safe send flag
  - Date: 2026-07-14
  - Session: CC-20260714-cr9k
  - What changed: Root cause of the 2026-07-14 flood of ~500 self-addressed emails to ali@colaberry.com: `backend/src/services/inbox/coraAgentService.ts` computed `const DRY_RUN = process.env.CORA_DRY_RUN === 'true'`, i.e. an UNSET flag defaulted to LIVE send, and `handleCoraInquiry` had zero loop guards — so a live Cora (prod ran CORA_DRY_RUN=false) replied to its OWN replies and to mailer-daemon bounce notices in the mailbox it also reads, looping every ~60s until Google rate-limited the account. Fix (this PR): (1) Sending is now OPT-IN — new pure `resolveDryRun()` returns dry-run for undefined/any value except the explicit string "false"; module-load `console.warn` when live send is enabled. So an unset/misconfigured flag can never send. (2) New pure `coraAutoReplySkipReason()` called at the top of `handleCoraInquiry` before any generation/send: skips our own send identity + mailbox (support@ and ali@, +tag/display-name normalized via new `normalizeEmailAddress()`), automated/bounce/no-reply senders (mailer-daemon, postmaster, no-reply, bounce), and RFC 3834 / common auto-responder headers (Auto-Submitted != no, Precedence: bulk|auto_reply|junk|list, X-Autoreply/X-Autorespond/X-Auto-Response-Suppress). Extracted a pure, tested detector `detectInboxUnsubscribeIntent(subject, body, fromAddress)` + `topReplyText()` into `unsubscribeEnforcementService.ts` with three defenses: (1) skip internal `@colaberry.com` senders; (2) match only the sender's OWN text, above any quoted/forwarded history (`topReplyText` cuts at `>`, "On … wrote:", "Forwarded message", Outlook divider, header block); (3) the bare word "unsubscribe" counts only in a SHORT reply (≤240 chars quote-stripped) — long bodies need an explicit imperative phrase (remove me / take me off / stop emailing / opt out / unsubscribe me / …), so a forwarded campaign footer is ignored. Subject-based detection (native Apple/Gmail List-Unsubscribe → subject "unsubscribe") is unchanged. `inboxStateManager` now calls the detector instead of inline keyword matching. Compliance: this only NARROWS matching for false positives — genuine requests (short reply, any imperative phrase, or the "unsubscribe" subject) still match, so no real opt-out is missed. (2) NEW `services/runtime/watchProgressService.ts` composes the math with the DB: `recordWatchBeat` (findOrCreate progress + read-merge-update `timeline_card_progress.analytics.watch` JSONB, certificateService pattern; returns {watched_pct,required_pct,met}) + `assertWatchRequirement` (the gate; early-returns if already completed → idempotent, throws `{status:422,code:'watch_requirement',watched_pct,required_pct}` below threshold). ## INCIDENT — Cora inbox mail loop, 1,800+ emails sent in ~20 minutes (BC #10095332194)
- [x] Fix the Cora self-reply mail loop + add loop-guard defenses
  - Date: 2026-07-14
  - Session: CC-20260713-t3v8
  - What changed: Ali reported ~1,800 emails in ~20 minutes from Cora (the support@colaberry.com AI inbox agent, migrated from Relevance AI, `CORA_DRY_RUN` apparently flipped live in prod outside this repo's history). Investigated (via a read-only Explore subagent, then confirmed by hand) and found a real, fully explainable self-reinforcing loop, not the old external Relevance AI system (zero trace of it remains in this codebase). Root cause: Cora sends replies through the same Gmail account she reads from; the inbox sync pulled in **Sent mail too** (no folder filter), so her own reply got re-ingested ~60s later as "new" inbound mail; the "is this a Cora inquiry?" check did a raw substring match across **every email header**, not just delivery headers — and her own `From:` line contains `support@colaberry.com`, so she re-matched her own rule and replied to herself, forever. Nothing anywhere in the pipeline deduped by thread or capped send volume. Four fixes, all defense-in-depth (any one alone would have stopped this specific incident; together they close the whole class of bug): (1) `hardRuleEngine.ts`'s `cora_0c` rule now checks only `To`/`Cc`/`Delivered-To`/`X-Original-To` — never a raw header-blob substring match — plus an explicit guard that a message FROM Cora's own configured address can never match. (2) `inboxSyncService.ts`'s Gmail sync query gained `-in:sent` so her own outgoing replies are never re-ingested as inbound mail in the first place. (3) New `cora_reply_logs` table (unique on `thread_key`) backs a reserve-then-send dedup in `coraAgentService.ts::handleCoraInquiry` — the thread is reserved via `findOrCreate` *before* generating or sending anything, so a duplicate/re-ingested inquiry for an already-answered thread is skipped without ever calling OpenAI or Gmail. (4) A new circuit breaker (`CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_MAX_SENDS`, default 20 per `CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_WINDOW_MINUTES`, default 10) checks recent `cora_reply_sent` audit-log volume before any send; once tripped, everything routes to the human INBOX instead of sending — checked *before* the dedup reservation so a tripped thread stays available for a real attempt once volume subsides, rather than being permanently marked "already handled" with no reply ever sent. Also refactored `CORA_DRY_RUN` from a module-load-time cached constant to a per-call `isDryRun()` check — a safe, incidental improvement (flips take effect without a process restart) that also removed the need for `jest.resetModules()` gymnastics in the new tests. Files: NEW backend/src/models/CoraReplyLog.ts, backend/src/seeds/migrations/20260714_add_cora_reply_log.sql, backend/src/services/inbox/__tests__/coraAgentService.test.ts; backend/src/services/inbox/hardRuleEngine.ts (narrowed header check + self-send guard), backend/src/services/inbox/inboxSyncService.ts (`-in:sent`), backend/src/services/inbox/coraAgentService.ts (dedup reservation, circuit breaker, `isDryRun()`), backend/src/models/index.ts (CoraReplyLog wiring), backend/src/services/inbox/__tests__/hardRuleEngine.test.ts (new `evaluateHardRules` describe block for the Cora rule, including the exact loop regression).
  - Verification: backend `tsc --noEmit` clean. New/extended tests — `hardRuleEngine.test.ts` gained an `evaluateHardRules — Cora support inbox rule` block (7 tests: happy-path match via To/Delivered-To/X-Original-To, the exact regression — a message with Cora's own `From:` header no longer matches `cora_0c`, a message FROM the support address never matches even if also addressed back to itself, and the guard still applies under a `CORA_SUPPORT_ADDRESS` override). New `coraAgentService.test.ts` (10 tests: first-time-thread happy path, the loop regression itself — a duplicate thread is skipped without ever calling OpenAI or Gmail, thread-id-missing falls back to message-id, circuit breaker trips at the ceiling and does not trip below it, a send failure still routes to a human, and dry-run mode skips the circuit breaker but still dedupes). 37/37 passing across both files. Full backend suite: 182/185 passing (of 186; 1 pre-existing skip), same 3 pre-existing unrelated failures as every prior entry this session. Migration applied to local dev DB, table + unique constraint verified via `\d`. **Live verification against real running code, deliberately WITHOUT triggering any real OpenAI/Gmail send** (the nature of this incident made that the correct boundary, not a shortcut): rebuilt `accelerator-dev-backend`, confirmed the compiled `inboxSyncService.js` actually contains `-in:sent` in the query string, then called the real `evaluateHardRules()` directly — a simulated self-sent email (from the real configured `CORA_SUPPORT_ADDRESS`, with a `From:` header containing that same address) correctly returned `matched:false`, while a genuine inbound inquiry to the same address still correctly returned `rule_id:"cora_0c"` — proving the fix doesn't break the feature while closing the loop. Separately called the real `CoraReplyLog.findOrCreate` twice with the same `thread_key` against real Postgres: first call `created:true`, second call `created:false` with the identical row id — dedup proven at the database level, not just asserted in a mock. Circuit breaker behavior is covered by the 6 passing unit tests (mocked audit-log count) and was not additionally live-fired, since doing so meaningfully would require generating real audit-log volume without a clear safe way to do that without also risking a real send path.
  - Notes: `CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_MAX_SENDS`/`CORA_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_WINDOW_MINUTES` are new optional env vars (default 20/10, no prod config change required to ship this fix). A generation or send failure leaves the thread's dedup reservation in place — deliberate: the existing `decideCoraDisposition` already routes those to the human INBOX, and auto-retrying a failed thread is exactly the class of risk this incident was about. This fix does not address whether the external Relevance AI integration is still active in parallel outside this codebase — that's outside this repo's visibility/control; confirming Relevance AI is fully decommissioned (or was never the actual source) is a separate action for Ali. Migration NOT yet applied to prod — this is the priority item to deploy once Kes/Ali confirm the immediate `CORA_DRY_RUN=true` mitigation is holding.

- [x] Build-log -> social drafter (#Colaberry stream) (BC #9985689786)
  - Date: 2026-07-14
  - Session: CC-20260713-t3v8
  - What changed: Ticket's Gherkin AC just says "produces a #Colaberry social draft" (singular), but its own "Build notes (precise)" line points to `TRAINING_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md` §3.7, which specifies 4 outputs (LinkedIn post, video script, architecture update, demo summary). First pass shipped text-only, reading the singular AC as "smallest version" — Kes corrected that this was my interpretation, not something the ticket said to defer, and asked for all 4. Rebuilt on that basis: each week's `BuildLogDraft` row (`project_id`+`week_number` unique) now holds 4 independently-generated, independently-approved sections (`linkedin_post`, `video_script`, `architecture_update`, `demo_summary`) inside `draft_content`, each with its own `{content, status, posted_at}` — dropped the earlier row-level `status`/`posted_at` columns entirely (redundant once status lives per-section; safe to change outright since this hadn't shipped anywhere). "A completed build-log entry" = a Tier-A `Artifact` row (`type:'build'`) in `submitted`/`reviewed` status — unchanged from the first pass. `draftBuildLogPost()` generates only whichever sections are still missing (per-section idempotency, not per-row): a section with existing content is never regenerated/re-billed; one section's LLM failure doesn't block the others (left ungenerated, retried next call); only throws if a call generates zero sections. `generateBuildLogDraftsForCompletedWeeks()` (weekly cron entry point, Mon 11:00 UTC) now skips a project/week only when *all 4* sections are done, otherwise fills in whatever's missing. `markBuildLogSectionStatus()` (renamed from `markBuildLogDraftStatus`) takes a `section` param, marks just that one posted/skipped, idempotent (re-posting doesn't bump `posted_at`), other sections untouched. Route `PATCH .../build-log-drafts/:draftId` now requires `{section, status}` in the body. No real LinkedIn/social API integration — "posted" stays a self-reported student action per the ticket's explicit no-auto-post trust control. Files: NEW backend/src/models/BuildLogDraft.ts, backend/src/services/buildLogDraftService.ts, backend/src/routes/buildLogDraftRoutes.ts, backend/src/seeds/migrations/20260714_add_build_log_drafts.sql, backend/src/__tests__/services/buildLogDraftService.test.ts; backend/src/models/index.ts (wiring + associations), backend/src/server.ts (route registration), backend/src/services/schedulerService.ts (new cron).
  - Verification: backend `tsc --noEmit` clean. `buildLogDraftService.test.ts` — 19/19 passing: all-4-sections happy path, `#Colaberry` normalization boundary, per-section idempotency (only missing sections regenerated, existing ones untouched — including a `posted` section staying `posted`), zero-LLM-call boundary when all 4 already exist, out-of-range week rejected pre-DB, missing project/incomplete week failure paths, one-section-fails-doesn't-block-the-others (failure isolation — the exact bug class this design targets), all-4-fail surfaces `UpstreamUnavailable` with no write, batch generator (drafts/skips-fully-done/isolates-per-project-failure), `markBuildLogSectionStatus` happy/idempotent/other-sections-untouched/unknown-section/missing-draft/not-yet-generated boundaries. Full backend suite: 3501/3602 passing (100 skipped), same 3 pre-existing unrelated failures as every prior entry this session (`seedCurriculumCourseLinks.test.ts`, `projectDnaService.test.ts`, `adminRoutes.test.ts`). **Caught a real production bug via live testing that the mocked unit tests could not have caught**: the first live-verification pass showed a genuine AI-drafted response in the HTTP body, but a direct `SELECT` against Postgres showed `content: null` for every section — the DB was never actually updated. Root cause: `draftBuildLogPost` read `draftRow.draft_content` by reference and mutated its nested fields in place before calling `.update()`; Sequelize's dirty-checking compares the incoming value against its own in-memory previous-value snapshot, and since both were now the same already-mutated object, it saw "no change" and silently skipped writing that column — the in-memory response looked correct while the database silently kept the stale `null` skeleton from the row's initial creation. Every re-run would have regenerated all 4 sections from scratch forever, burning 4 real LLM calls per call with zero persistence — exactly the kind of idempotency violation the repo's CLAUDE.md calls a production defect, not a nit. Fixed by deep-cloning (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`) before mutating, so the object passed to `.update()` is never reference-identical to Sequelize's tracked previous value. Re-verified against real Postgres end-to-end: generated all 4 sections for a real project/week → confirmed via direct SQL that `content` was genuinely persisted (not just in the API response) → called generate again → `generated_at` and all content byte-identical before/after (true idempotency, zero re-billed LLM calls, confirmed via DB read not just HTTP response) → marked `linkedin_post` posted → `posted_at` set, `video_script` untouched → re-posted `linkedin_post` → `posted_at` unchanged (idempotent) → marked `video_script` skipped independently → `architecture_update`/`demo_summary` still `draft`, proving true per-section independence → invalid section name rejected 400 → a JWT for a different enrollment got `404` on the same project's drafts, confirming per-student isolation held through the rewrite. Migration dropped/recreated on local dev DB (`accelerator_dev1`) to match the new schema (row-level status/posted_at columns removed). The weekly cron's registration itself was not live-fired (`startScheduler()` gated behind `env.enableFollowUpScheduler`, off by design in dev to avoid also triggering the health monitor's real Synthflow voice call) — confirmed correct via `tsc` + structural match to neighboring cron blocks only.
  - Notes: This is now the full §3.7 scope — no formats remain deferred. No real LinkedIn/social API posting integration exists; "posted" is self-reported. Migration NOT yet applied to prod. Left the demo build-log draft and its source test artifact in the dev DB as legitimate feature-generated data. The Sequelize JSONB-mutation gotcha here (read-by-reference, mutate-in-place, then `.update()` silently no-ops) is worth remembering for any future JSONB field — mocked unit tests cannot catch it since a bare `jest.fn()` doesn't replicate real Sequelize change-detection; only a live DB round-trip surfaces it, which is why the live-verification step in this repo's process is load-bearing, not a formality.

  - What changed: The classroom back-restore (PR #339) was landing the student at the TOP, not their saved scroll position. Root cause: the feed's card thumbnails (video/podcast posters) load AFTER the cards render, so at remount the document is short; the naive `requestAnimationFrame(requestAnimationFrame(() => window.scrollTo(0, savedY)))` fired before the images grew the page back to height, so scrollTo clamped near the top. Fix in `frontend/src/pages/portal/ClassroomPage.tsx`: new module-level `restoreScroll(targetY)` polls per animation frame until `document.documentElement.scrollHeight - innerHeight >= targetY` (i.e. images have restored the page to the height it had when saved), then scrolls once; bails immediately on user `wheel`/`touchstart` so it never fights the student, and caps at 3s so a genuinely-shorter feed doesn't spin. Because savedY was captured in the fully-loaded layout and we now restore only in the fully-loaded layout, the pixel offset is accurate. The restore effect calls `restoreScroll(snap.scrollY || 0)` in place of the double-rAF.

- [x] Classroom scroll-restore: save scroll LIVE (fixes the real "back always lands at top" bug)
  - Date: 2026-07-19
  - Session: CC-20260718-b3k9
  - What changed: THE actual root cause of "back sends me to the top" (three prior fixes — PR #339 save/restore, #371 wait-for-images — never moved it). The snapshot was written in a useEffect UNMOUNT CLEANUP: `useEffect(() => () => writeViewSnapshot({week, scrollY: window.scrollY}), [])`. But useEffect cleanups are PASSIVE — React runs them AFTER it has already swapped ClassroomPage's DOM out for the workspace and App-level ScrollToTop has zeroed the window — so `window.scrollY` read ~0 at that point. Every save recorded `scrollY: 0`, so every restore faithfully restored to 0 (the top); no restore-side fix could ever help. Fix in `frontend/src/pages/portal/ClassroomPage.tsx`: replaced the unmount-cleanup save with a live throttled `scroll` listener (active while `uiState==='ready'`, one write/frame via rAF) that persists `{week, scrollY}` WHILE the page is still mounted and scrolled — capturing the real position. Kept the wait-for-height `restoreScroll` from #371 for the restore side; the two now compose correctly.
  - Verification: frontend `tsc --noEmit` — zero errors in ClassroomPage.tsx (junctioned typecheck). Diagnostic confirmation: on the live (pre-fix) bundle, `sessionStorage.getItem('classroom-view')` shows `scrollY: 0` even after scrolling far — proving the save side; with this fix it shows the real scroll offset.
  - Notes: Built in isolated worktree on branch `workstream/classroom-scroll-save-fix` off `origin/main`. Frontend-only → deploy nginx. Also ruled out (this session) as NOT the cause: inner scroll container (the classroom scrolls the WINDOW — `.te-shell` min-height:100vh, no overflow anywhere on the feed path), service worker (none), Cloudflare stale HTML (index.html is no-store/DYNAMIC, serves the current bundle). Lesson: never read scroll position in a passive-effect unmount cleanup — capture it live.

Moved persistence to the HOST: new `useDeepDiveHost` hook (replaces `useFieldGuideUpload`) persists read section-ids + copied to the app's real localStorage keyed by cardId and restores them into the guide via a `ready`→`restore` postMessage handshake. Consolidated the drawer + workspace deep-dive listeners into this one hook. Guide now posts `ids`/`copied` and applies host `restore` (read+copy+upload).
  - Why: Ali — "use [the design-system colors] for the Field Guides… I don't understand the design and how you just created a logo"; "when you've gotten the progress to 100% it doesn't free up the Complete button"; "when I reached 100% and then went to my workspace, the progress meter reset.
