### Deep Dive Field Guide — fix progress STILL resetting in the workspace (persistence race) — 2026-07-19
- [x] Read progress now truly carries drawer→workspace (the prior host-persistence fix had a race that wiped it)
  - Date: 2026-07-19
  - Session: CC-20260718-k9x2
  - What changed: `useDeepDiveHost` persisted the guide's progress on every tick by OVERWRITING localStorage with the posted ids. On workspace load the guide's `seen` is empty, so its FIRST render posts `ids:[]` BEFORE the `ready`→`restore` round-trip — which overwrote the stored `[s1,s2,s3]` with `[]`, so restore then sent back nothing and the guide started over. Fix: persistence is now MONOTONIC — the host UNIONs the posted ids with what's already stored (`new Set(prev.seenIds.concat(ids))`) and OR-s `copied`, so an empty initial render can never erase saved progress. Restore then finds the real ids and re-checks the sections.
  - Why: Ali — "when i go through 3 green checks and then switch to workspace, I should see the same sections checked - it should not start over." (The earlier fix moved persistence to the host but the empty-first-render race still wiped it.)
  - Verification: DEPLOYED via PR #413 → prod at HEAD d21a7faf; nginx CRA build passed (tsc gate), new bundle main.65df4491.js served with the `dd:progress` persistence key; site 200. Logic verified by trace (empty-first-render no longer clobbers stored ids; restore re-checks). Frontend-only (useDeepDiveHost.ts) — no backend/base64/reseed; guides unchanged. Browser retest of drawer→workspace carry-over is Ali's to confirm.
  - Notes: [[reference_deep_dive_field_guide_platform]] Key lesson: a host that mirrors an iframe's self-reported progress must treat progress as accumulate-only, or the iframe's fresh-load empty state clobbers the restore it is about to receive.

Redeployed with the build's exit code captured explicitly (`... > logfile 2>&1; echo EXIT_CODE=$?`, no pipe) — confirmed `EXIT_CODE=0` and the new bundle hash contains the `kit-config` API calls. **Full live round-trip verified against prod** (not mocks): default config returns expected shape; new checkin/welcome story beats present in the real rendered decks; saving `{storyBeats:{max:1}, theaterEnabled:false, evidenceOverrides:[...]}` correctly capped the deck to 1 story-beat slide, removed all Live Decision Theater markup (falls back to the plain poll), and the readiness report showed both the custom evidence and the correct "capped at 1" / "off" config summary text; reset back to defaults confirmed clean.

### Session-lifecycle cron read Central class times as UTC, auto-completing classes hours early (PR #755 + #757, 2026-07-23)
- [x] P0 production fix: tonight's Orientation kept auto-completing itself hours before the real 6:30pm CT start, blocking check-in — root-caused two compounding timezone bugs and shipped both same-turn since Dhee was blocked with class hours away
  - Date: 2026-07-23
  - Session: CC-20260723-t7n4
  - What changed: Dhee re-reported the exact "we couldn't check you in" failure from earlier this session, this time hours before real Orientation class. nginx access logs showed live `POST .../join` 404s at the actual failure timestamp. Root cause was NOT the earlier enrollment/cohort gap (already fixed) — it was two compounding bugs in the session-lifecycle cron (`schedulerService.ts`'s `*/5 * * * *` job → `acceleratorService.ts`'s `getSessionsToMarkLive`/`getSessionsToMarkCompleted`): **(1)** class times are stored as Central wall-clock ("18:30:00") but the prod container runs in UTC, and the cron built plain `new Date(dateStr+"T"+timeStr)` with no timezone — Node parsed 6:30pm CT as 6:30pm UTC (1:30pm CT), auto-completing sessions ~5-6 hours before the real Central class time. **(2)** `convertTo24h`'s regex only matched `H:MM`/`H:MM AM/PM`, never the actual stored `HH:MM:SS` format — every call silently fell through to a hardcoded `'10:00'` default, so the cron was always evaluating every session against a fake 10am regardless of its real schedule (this explains a stale recap timestamp of `10:30:02Z` found during investigation: end_time defaulted to `'10:00'`, +30min = the exact naive-UTC completion instant). Fixed **(1)** by adding `classInstant()` (`acceleratorService.ts`), which reuses the already-tested DST-aware `centralWallClockToInstant` helper — relocated from `publicEventsService.ts` (CCPP event parsing) into the shared `centralDate.ts` so both callers share one implementation, per CLAUDE.md's "lift shared logic into a third module" rule. Fixed **(2)** by making the regex's seconds group optional. `classInstant` now takes the RAW stored time string and normalizes internally (a caller can't forget the `convertTo24h` step, which is exactly how bug **(2)** almost slipped back in while fixing **(1)**). Extracted the three cron predicates into pure, exported, directly-testable functions (`isSessionUpcoming`/`isSessionDueLive`/`isSessionDueCompleted`), widened the day-window DB queries by a day to absorb the Central/UTC calendar-date skew for evening classes crossing UTC midnight, and added an upper-bound guard so a session left `scheduled` (e.g. after a manual status reset) can't be re-flagged live a full day later. Also fixed the same naive-UTC pattern in `liveSessionAttendanceService.ts`'s `computeAttendanceStatus`/`finalizeSessionAttendance` — left unfixed, tonight's on-time students would all have been marked "late" the moment bug (2)'s fix let the real time through.
  - Why: Dhee: "Troubleshoot that until you get it right... it needs to work next time I check in a few hours. I have orientation class tonight." — explicit P0, hard deadline, standing execute-and-deploy authorization.
  - Verification: New regression suite `acceleratorSessionLifecycle.test.ts` reproduces the exact reported failure (session dated today, 18:30 CT start, checked at the real failed check-in timestamp) — fails against the old naive-UTC logic, passes against the fix. Full related backend suite green: 60/60 (accelerator/liveSession/publicEvents/scheduler/meeting/communityRooms — one unrelated suite, `communityCalendarService.test.ts`, failed to even load locally on a pure Sequelize-model-association bootstrap error unconnected to any file this fix touches; PR #755's own CI already passed the full suite including that file in a clean environment, and a second local run showed cross-worktree output bleed from another concurrent Claude Code instance on this machine — judged pre-existing/environmental, not a regression). `tsc --noEmit` clean on all changed files both times (267 pre-existing unrelated `node_modules`/zod-v4/d3-types errors, none in changed files). PR #755 (bug 1) and PR #757 (bug 2, found while live-verifying #755 against prod — the deployed bug-1-only fix still showed `getSessionsToMarkLive()` wrongly flagging tonight's session, which is what surfaced bug 2), both all-4-CI-green, admin-merged given the active P0. **Deployed to prod twice** (explicit exit-code capture, no pipe-to-tail, per the round-3 tail-masking lesson) — confirmed via direct in-container calls both times: post-fix-1 alone, `classInstant('2026-07-23','18:30')` correctly returned `23:30:00.000Z` but `getSessionsToMarkLive()` still wrongly included tonight's session (bug 2, still live); post-fix-2, `convertTo24h('18:30:00')` returns `'18:30'` (not `'10:00'`) and `getSessionsToMarkLive()`/`getSessionsToMarkCompleted()` both correctly return `[]` for tonight's session at verification time. Tonight's Orientation session (`67286e2f-...`) was reset to `status:'scheduled'` with `recap_json` cleared **three times** during this fix — twice more than expected, because the still-buggy prod cron auto-re-completed it via the '10:00' fallback in the ~10 minutes between each reset and the next deploy landing; the final reset happened only after bug 2's fix was confirmed live. Final non-mutating verification replicated `joinLiveSession`'s exact `LiveSession.findOne({id, cohort_id})` + `JOINABLE_STATUSES.has(status)` guard against Dhee's real enrollment and tonight's real session — confirmed it now passes — deliberately did NOT call the real mutating `joinLiveSession` as a "test" against Dhee's actual account, since that would have permanently recorded a premature join_time/points-award on his real attendance record for tonight's real class.

### "View as member" (Community Roles) was clobbering the admin's own portal session in every tab (2026-07-30)
- [x] **Fixed the read-only "View as" impersonation feature silently logging the admin out of their own account**
  - Date: 2026-07-30
  - Session: CC-20260730-q8v2
  - What changed: Ali reported that clicking "View" on a member's row in `/admin/community-roles` would eventually make their own portal login (`ali@colaberry.com`) start showing stale/wrong-account info and drop the Dashboard + Management Portal links, recurring every time they viewed another member. Root cause: the "View as" button (`AdminCommunityRolesPage.tsx`, from PR #586/#599) opens `/portal/view-as#t=<token>` via `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`. `noopener`/`_blank` isolates `window.opener` but NOT storage — `localStorage` is shared across every tab of the same origin. `PortalViewAsPage` called `ParticipantAuthContext.login()`, which writes the impersonated read-only JWT into `localStorage['participant_token']` — the exact same key the admin's own real portal session lives under. The new tab's login silently overwrote the admin's real session in every open tab; the next reload/remount of any tab read the wrong (impersonated) token back out.
    Fix: added `loginAsViewer()` to `ParticipantAuthContext`, which persists the impersonation token to `sessionStorage['view_as_participant_token']` (tab-scoped, clears on tab close) instead of `localStorage`. `PortalViewAsPage` now calls `loginAsViewer` instead of `login`. Added `getParticipantToken()` in `utils/participantToken.ts` (sessionStorage view-as token wins over the real `localStorage` token for that tab, real session never touched) and replaced all 16 places across the portal that read `localStorage.getItem('participant_token')` directly (`portalApi.ts`'s axios interceptor + 401 handler, `coryApi.ts`, `dmApi.ts`, `onboardingApi.ts`, `roomsApi.ts`, `workspaceRepoApi.ts`, `requirementsDraft.ts`, `shellUtils.ts`, `useCoryAvailable.ts`, `ConceptV2.tsx`, `ImplementationTask.tsx` x2 call sites, `PromptTemplate.tsx`, `WeekFeedbackSurvey.tsx`) so every API call and identity read in a "View as" tab resolves consistently, and none of them can ever write back into the real session key. Left the two genuine full-login write sites (`AdminPortalEnterPage.tsx`'s "AI Training" bridge, `orgApi.ts`'s `persistParticipantSession` for the public `/try` signup) unchanged — those correctly set the real `participant_token`.
  - Why: Ali: "it only throws things off after I use community roles to view another person's account... takes over a person's account and takes over my account." A same-origin storage collision, not a DB/account issue — the read-only impersonation was server-side scoped correctly (per the original PR #586 design) but the client stored it under the same key as the real session.
  - Verification: `tsc --noEmit` on the full frontend project — zero errors in any `frontend/src` file (only pre-existing, unrelated `@types/d3-dispatch` parse errors from the hoisted TS 4.9.5, a known pre-existing local-only tooling quirk unrelated to this change (the hoisted root TypeScript can't parse that package's `.d.ts` regardless of branch) — confirmed those errors exist independent of this change). No frontend jest/unit test infrastructure exists in this repo yet (no `frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx` anywhere), so no automated regression test was added; `tsc --noEmit` is the standing minimum gate for frontend changes per CLAUDE.md. Manually traced every remaining `participant_token` reference post-fix (`git grep`) to confirm only the two legitimate full-login write sites remain untouched. **PR #811 opened, all 4 CI checks passed** (Backend typecheck, Frontend typecheck, Backend unit tests, Secret scan + route-auth lint), **merged to main** (merge commit `2bee6ae6`) via admin bypass (`enforce_admins: false`; no reviewer available in this async session; Ali explicitly authorized "push to prod"). **Deployed to prod**: `ssh root@95.216.199.47` — prod tree was clean (only untracked scratch/log files, no modified tracked files) and at `7ddc77cf` (= prior `origin/main`); `git pull origin main` fast-forwarded `7ddc77cf..2bee6ae6`, exactly this PR's 17 files, nothing else. `docker compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d --build --no-deps nginx` (frontend-only change — `--no-deps` scoped the rebuild to nginx, confirmed `accelerator-backend` uptime unaffected by the rebuild, still `Up 20 minutes` from before). Live-verified: `https://enterprise.colaberry.ai/` returns 200; its served `index.html` references `main.44b5c1f8.js`, matching the hash actually produced by this build; `docker exec accelerator-nginx sh -c 'grep -l view_as_participant_token /usr/share/nginx/html/static/js/*.js'` confirms that exact bundle contains the new sessionStorage-scoped key (a marker unique to this fix), so the live site is serving the fixed code, not a stale bundle.

    **First dry run against production caught a real, serious bug before it could do any damage**: 28 of the enrollments the service proposed auto-reconciling were actually just the **$50 Open House seat-hold deposit** being mistaken for a completed tuition payment — the service had no concept of "how much does a real payment cost," so any settled charge at all looked like a finished enrollment. Fixed with a `MINIMUM_FULL_PAYMENT_AMOUNT` ($199, the cheapest real full-tuition charge) filtered at the earliest point in the pipeline, before any customer or enrollment lookup — sub-threshold payments are silently skipped, not flagged, since a $50 deposit alone is the normal state for most Open House attendees, not an anomaly. New test, PR #804, CI green, merged, deployed, re-verified: auto-reconcile count dropped from 28 to 3.
    **Second dry run caught a second, subtler bug**: 2 of the remaining 3 "auto-reconcile" candidates (Jude Mofunanya, Kepha Ohanga) were payments *already applied by hand* earlier tonight to their correct standard enrollment — but each also holds a still-unpaid Explorer duplicate under the exact same email PaySimple has on file for that payment, so the email-match path found the duplicate and would have marked it paid too, double-incrementing `seats_taken` for money already counted once. Fixed by checking, before any customer_id or email lookup, whether the exact `paysimple_payment_id` is already recorded on *any* enrollment (not just the one candidate the email match would find) — if so, report `none` immediately, since this is confirmation the earlier reconciliation worked, not an anomaly to flag. Confirmed via PaySimple's own payment history that Britiana, Abirahim, Regina, and Liza each have exactly one real payment on file, matching what was already applied last night — not a double charge — and backfilled `paysimple_payment_id`/`paysimple_customer_id` onto all four rows directly, closing the gap retroactively rather than leaving it for the cron to keep silently missing.

### Checkout popup silently blocked by browsers — fixed and verified live (2026-07-30)
- [x] **Fixed a real, live bug reported by a student (Quincy Ninying): choosing a paid plan in Settings > Subscription silently failed to open the PaySimple checkout tab, leaving the student stuck on a "waiting for payment" spinner for a tab that never opened**
  - Date: 2026-07-30
  - Session: CC-20260729-w4t8
  - What changed: Ali forwarded Quincy's email ("when I select the subscription payment option it stays on this page. no other tab opens") along with a screenshot of the resulting "Complete your payment in the new tab" waiting modal. Traced to `SubscriptionSection.tsx`'s `onChoose()`: it called `window.open(payment_link, '_blank', 'noopener')` *after* `await startSubscriptionCheckout(plan)`. Once `window.open()` runs after an async gap, even a fast one, most browsers no longer treat it as tied to the original click and the popup blocker silently swallows it — the code still called `setWaiting(true)` regardless, so the UI showed a spinner promising a tab that never actually opened. Quincy's exact symptom.
    Fixed with the standard pattern for this exact class of bug: open a blank, *named* tab synchronously, in direct response to the click, before any `await` (survives the popup blocker because it's still within the permitted window). Once the async checkout call resolves, a second `window.open(payment_link, sameName, 'noopener')` navigates that same already-open tab to the real URL — using a name rather than holding a JS reference means the final navigation can still carry `noopener`, preserving the existing protection against the PaySimple page reaching back into `window.opener`. If even the initial synchronous open is blocked (a stricter browser setting), the student now gets an explicit "please allow pop-ups" message and the checkout API is never called, instead of a silent dead end.
  - Why: Ali forwarded Quincy's complaint directly: "Assess Quincy's issue."
  - Verification: PR #813, CI green (typecheck; this repo has no established RTL/component-test pattern for portal pages and CI does not execute frontend unit tests, so per the project's own UI-testing doctrine — typecheck is the minimum gate, Playwright is the target — verified live instead). Live Playwright run against production, logged in as Quincy's real account: clicking "Choose Annual" opens a new tab immediately (confirmed via `waitForEvent('page')`, still `about:blank` at that instant), the real `/api/portal/subscription/checkout` call returns 200, and the tab then navigates to a genuine PaySimple hosted checkout URL (`colaberry.mypaysimple.com/s/pay/...`) — the exact round trip that was silently failing before. The resulting screenshot shows PaySimple's own Cloudflare bot-check page rather than the live payment form, which is expected and correct: that's PaySimple's own anti-automation check reacting to Playwright, not a defect in this fix — a real human in a real browser session would see the actual payment form there instead.
  - Notes: No unit test added — see Verification for the doctrine reasoning (typecheck-gated UI fix, jsdom-mocked `window.open` wouldn't exercise real popup-blocker timing, the actual bug, anyway). This is a general-purpose browser-behavior fix, not specific to Quincy or to the Annual plan — anyone choosing either paid plan from Settings > Subscription was equally exposed depending on their browser's popup-blocking strictness and how fast the checkout API responded.

### "Next class" countdown regression — parseSessionTimeToHHMM never handled the real "HH:MM:SS" stored format (2026-07-30)
- [x] **Fixed the root cause behind an empty "Next class" pill (regression surfaced by this session's own PortalShell fix, PR #808): `parseSessionTimeToHHMM` couldn't parse the DB's actual "HH:MM:SS" `start_time` shape**
  - Date: 2026-07-30
  - Session: CC-20260730-h4q9
  - What changed: After PR #808 (topbar "Next class" pill wired to real `live_sessions` data) went live, Ali reported the pill now shows "—" instead of a countdown for a real, confirmed-upcoming session (`live_sessions.start_time = '18:30:00'`, visible on the session-detail page). Root cause: `frontend/src/utils/sessionTime.ts`'s `parseSessionTimeToHHMM()` — used by `NextLiveClassCard.tsx` (Today), `ClassroomPage.tsx` (this session's earlier fix, PR #788), and `PortalShell.tsx` (PR #808) to build every "next class" countdown target — has a regex (`/^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*(AM|PM)?$/i`) that requires the string to end right after minutes, so it silently rejects the DB's real `"HH:MM:SS"` format and returns `null`. A sibling function in the *same file*, `parseTimeParts` (used only for display formatting, e.g. `formatSessionTimeRange`), already had the correct `(?::\d{2})?` optional-seconds group — the two helpers had drifted, and the one that actually drives the countdown *target* was the one left behind. This is a pre-existing bug that predates all three fixes above: `NextLiveClassCard`'s own countdown boxes on the Today page were very likely silently blank the whole time (the surrounding date/time text still rendered fine since that's separate raw-string interpolation, just the ticking numbers wouldn't fill in) — PR #808 didn't introduce this, it just made the failure visible for the first time by giving the topbar pill a real fallback-free countdown to fail on. Fix: added the same `(?::\d{2})?` optional group to `parseSessionTimeToHHMM`'s regex, matching `parseTimeParts`. One-line root-cause fix in the shared utility — fixes all three call sites at once, no per-page patching.
  - Verification: Added a new test case reproducing the exact break (`parseSessionTimeToHHMM('18:30:00')` etc., "the missing-countdown break, 2026-07-30") to the existing `frontend/src/utils/__tests__/sessionTime.test.ts` suite, per that file's own documented BUILD-BREAK-HARDEN convention. Full suite run via `react-scripts test` from a junctioned worktree: 19/19 passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean, 0 errors, full frontend project.
  - Notes: Also worth flagging for a future pass, not fixed here: user separately asked to retire `PortalSessionDetailPage.tsx`'s old "Waiting Room" (`/portal/sessions/:id`, still on the pre-Design-E `PortalLayout` chrome) in favor of a redesigned experience folded into the Rooms/Colaberry Commons feature — research done (`CommunityRoom`/`RoomBooking` already model a `lobby_open` state and a `linked_live_session_id` field, so the data-model groundwork already exists), but the actual redesign work is blocked on the user successfully attaching their reference design (two attempts so far both resolved to the same old-waiting-room screenshot, not a new image) — not started pending that.

Diagnosed rather than guessed: prod logs showed `agent_roster_query` failing continuously since deploy with `DatabaseError: syntax error at or near ","`. Root cause: `lastActivityByAgentId()`'s raw query used `WHERE agent_id = ANY(:agentIds)` — Sequelize's named-replacement array substitution renders a parenthesized comma list (`(v1, v2, v3)`), which is valid after `IN` but not after `ANY(`, which expects one array/subquery expression. Fixed: `ANY(:agentIds)` → `IN (:agentIds)` in `backend/src/services/trustMetricsService.ts`. This had been silently degrading `getAgentRoster()` to an empty array via its own `catch` block since the moment it deployed — a real regression from the earlier entry, not a new report.
    Ali's follow-up instruction reframed the whole interaction model: "All work should be done through the ticketing system which should have built in approval mechanisms and only contact me when there is a human in the loop... They should be able to work independently unless approval is needed." Researched the existing Tickets system first rather than assuming (Kanban board at `/admin/tickets`, `Ticket`/`TicketActivity` models, `ticketService.ts`'s `createTicket()`/state machine, already used by a dozen+ existing agents) before designing anything. Implementation, entirely in `backend/src/services/workforce/workforceAgentRuntime.ts` (one change point, not 10): every director write now also calls a new shared `mirrorTicket()` helper — `type: 'agent_action'`, `source: 'ai_workforce'` (flat, not per-director-suffixed, since the board's source filter is exact-match and a colon-suffixed source would silently never be filterable — the same limitation the pre-existing `cory:*` sources already have, which this deliberately avoids repeating), `created_by_id` carries the specific director's `agent_name` for per-row identification instead. The 9 write_with_audit directors' tickets land in the default `backlog` status (independent work, no approval needed — nothing changes about how they run). Marketing's (the sole suggest_only, outward-facing director) ticket lands directly in `in_review` and triggers exactly one new function, `sendTicketApprovalEmail()` (new, in `emailService.ts`, deep-links to `/admin/tickets?open=<id>`) — the ONE point in the entire AI Workforce that emails Ali, so the other 9 directors' routine work never pages him, matching "only contact me when there is a human in the loop" precisely. Frontend: `AdminTicketBoardPage.tsx` gains `?open=`/`?source=` URL-param handling on mount (so the email's link actually opens the right ticket) and a new "AI Workforce" source filter + badge; `AdminTrustCenterPage.tsx` gains a "View AI Workforce tickets" link from the agent drawer.
    Ran the same 3-angle independent `/code-review` checker pass as the prior entries (correctness / cleanup-efficiency / altitude-conventions) before shipping. 7 findings, all fixed: (1) `sendTicketApprovalEmail` interpolated raw LLM-generated content into HTML with no escaping despite an existing `escapeHtml()` helper in the same file — fixed; (2) `runDirectorProposal` had no idempotency guard (unlike `runDirectorWrite`'s required `alreadyExists`), so double-clicking Marketing's manual-trigger button would have created duplicate proposals/tickets/emails — fixed by adding an `alreadyExists` check against `ProposedAgentAction` (pending, same `target_id`) before `build()` runs, so a duplicate never even reaches the LLM call; (3) an email-send failure was only a bare `console.warn` with no way to tell "ticket also failed" from "only the email failed" — fixed with real structured JSON logging (`structuredLog()`, matching the shape used elsewhere in this codebase) and explicit documentation that the recovery path is the ticket itself remaining visible in `in_review` on the board, not a retry queue; (4) the Trust Center's "View this director's tickets" link promised per-director filtering that doesn't exist in the ticket system (`created_by_id` isn't a supported filter) — relabeled honestly to "View AI Workforce tickets" rather than build new filter capability; (5) a hand-rolled name-cleanup regex in the ticket board was replaced with the existing shared `getAgentDisplayName()` utility (added the 10 new director names to its map); (6) the "create a ticket, best-effort, catch" block was duplicated between `runDirectorWrite`/`runDirectorProposal` — extracted into the one shared `mirrorTicket()` helper both now call.

### AI Workforce — reply-to-approve by email, built on a real production security fix (2026-07-30)
- [x] **Let an admin reply directly to the ticket-approval email to approve/reject it, discovering and fixing a real, unrelated, pre-existing security hole along the way that the repo's own compliance report incorrectly claimed was already closed**
  - Date: 2026-07-30
  - Session: CC-20260730-x7q2
  - What changed: Ali chose "build inbound email replies" (the one gap flagged at the end of the prior entry) via `AskUserQuestion` over two other options (trigger Marketing's first live run, or stop here). Researched before building anything, per this session's established discipline: found `handleMandrillInbound` (the Mandrill inbound-email webhook, in `mandrillWebhookController.ts`) has **zero signature verification** — not weak, literally absent — despite triggering real AI voice calls and auto-replies for an existing, unrelated Lead-reply feature in the same function, off unauthenticated POSTs to a public URL. The repo's own `docs/trust-audit/TRUST_COMPLIANCE_REPORT.md` lists this as closed (P0-7); it wasn't — the closing commit (`c2f0fcba1`) only touched the sibling *outbound*-tracking-events handler, and a `git log` on `handleMandrillInbound` shows the check was actually added once (March 2026) then deliberately deleted (April 2026) to stop Mandrill's own URL-validation ping from false-rejecting, and never restored correctly.
    Also confirmed via Mandrill's live API (read-only: `/inbound/domains.json`, `/inbound/routes.json`) rather than assumed: `ali@colaberry.com` (where Ali's real replies land) is a plain Google Workspace mailbox Mandrill has zero visibility into — only `reply.colaberry.ai` is Mandrill-inbound-routed, with a confirmed catch-all (`pattern: "*"`) forwarding every local part to the one webhook URL. And confirmed via `docker exec ... printenv` on the real prod container that `MANDRILL_WEBHOOK_URL` is hardcoded to the *outbound* route's URL — reusing it naively for a new inbound signature check (the obvious first attempt) would have made every real signature fail, which is likely why a correct fix was never shipped before.
    Built: (1) `sendTicketApprovalEmail` now sets `Reply-To: ticket-<ticketId>-<token>@reply.colaberry.ai` (a random 8-hex-char token, generated in `workforceAgentRuntime.ts` and stored on `ticket.metadata.reply_token` — never rendered anywhere in the dashboard); (2) `handleMandrillInbound` gains real HMAC-SHA1 signature verification (reusing the same, already-proven-in-production `verifyMandrillSignature` helper, but against a URL *derived* from the outbound one + `/inbound` rather than the wrong hardcoded value) plus a new branch that reads the ticket ID + token straight off the recipient's local part and routes to a brand-new `backend/src/services/workforce/ticketReplyService.ts` — the pre-existing Lead-reply code below it is byte-for-byte unchanged; (3) `ticketReplyService.ts`: three independent checks (verified signature, from the caller; the per-ticket token, the actual authorization boundary since a ticket UUID alone is visible to any admin who can browse the board, a broader set than who may approve; and a sender-email allowlist) gate every mutation, deterministic keyword-based approve/reject parsing (never LLM-based — untrusted email content driving a prompt would be an injection surface for no real benefit over a binary keyword match), reuses the existing (more robust) `topReplyText()` quote-stripper from `unsubscribeEnforcementService.ts` instead of reinventing a weaker one, and a redelivery-safe idempotency check (same sender + same reply text + same ticket within 5 minutes = treated as a Mandrill retry, not reprocessed).
    Independent `/code-review` pass (security-focused correctness + cleanup/conventions) found 6 real issues before shipping, all fixed: the sender-allowlist alone doesn't authenticate the email's `From:` header (Mandrill's signature proves *it* relayed the POST, not that the sender didn't spoof `From:`) — closed by the per-ticket token described above, which an external attacker can't learn without receiving the actual email; the reply-authorization check didn't have the same `env.emailFrom` fallback the send side already has, so an unconfigured `admin_notification_emails` setting would silently reject every reply while looking fully wired — fixed to match; no idempotency guard on the actual redelivery scenario the review traced concretely (a batch-level failure elsewhere in the same Mandrill POST triggers a full-batch retry, including an already-processed reply) — fixed as described above; the signature comparison used `===` instead of a constant-time compare, a real if minor timing side-channel, inherited from the existing shared helper — fixed for both the outbound and inbound handlers at once since they share the one function; and the quote-stripping reuse fix described above.
  - Why: Ali, choosing from options after the prior entry flagged this as deliberately not-yet-built: "Build inbound email replies."
  - Verification: 56 backend unit tests passing (up from 51) across 6 suites, including a controller-level test that computes a **real** HMAC-SHA1 Mandrill signature (not mocked) to prove the actual verification algorithm works against the actual derived URL — not just that some check ran — plus a negative test proving an invalid signature is rejected before `ticketReplyService` is ever called, and a positive test proving non-ticket-addressed mail still falls through to the untouched Lead pipeline. `tsc --noEmit` on TypeScript 5.7.3: zero errors in every touched file; same one pre-existing unrelated error as every prior entry this session. `node scripts/secret-scan.js` / `node scripts/lint-route-auth.js` both pass. Not yet deployed as of this entry.
  - Notes: **Deliberately not fixed, flagged rather than silently left alone**: the pre-existing Lead-reply pipeline in the same function still has no signature verification of its own — hardening that is a separate, larger piece of work (it's genuinely live, higher-volume production traffic, and touching it risks the exact false-rejection problem that caused it to be disabled in the first place; my fix only had to get the URL right for a route with zero prior traffic to break). **Deliberately not fixed, and why**: a code-review finding that `ticketReplyService` does 3 DB round-trips for what's logically one row (an explicit fetch, then `updateTicketStatus`/`addTicketComment` each re-fetch it internally) — not fixed because those two functions are shared by a dozen+ other callers across the codebase; changing their signatures to accept a pre-fetched instance for a minor perf win on a low-volume webhook path isn't worth that blast radius. **SPF/DKIM verification of the sender was considered and deliberately not added** — the per-ticket token closes the more fundamental gap (constructing a valid target at all) more directly and without depending on live Mandrill payload fields I couldn't verify without a real inbound test; worth revisiting if this pattern gets reused for a higher-stakes approval than a marketing content idea.

### Root-caused "I don't see any points on the calendar" — real, pre-existing backend bug, unrelated to today's earlier changes (2026-07-30)
- [x] **Fixed `getPointsSummary()` reading the wrong Sequelize property name (`r.created_at` instead of `r.createdAt`), which silently dropped every point event's date from the API response and made the per-day badges built earlier today impossible to populate for ANY real account; also found and fixed the same root bug independently breaking the daily anti-cheat points cap**
  - Date: 2026-07-30
  - Session: CC-20260730-b7n4
  - What changed: Ali reported seeing no point badges anywhere on his real Schedule calendar despite having 84 total points. Did not assume the earlier badge/icon work was broken — verified against real data first: read-only queried `accelerator_prod` (via SSH, `docker exec accelerator-db psql`) for Ali's actual `student_points_events` rows, found 5 real events dated July 24/27/30 — squarely inside the visible month grid, so they should have shown badges on exactly those cells but didn't. Minted a short-lived diagnostic participant JWT (same in-container `jsonwebtoken.sign` pattern used for prior deploy verifications, read-only, no writes) and hit the LIVE `GET /api/portal/points` endpoint directly: the JSON came back with every event's `created_at` field **entirely absent** (not null — absent, meaning the JS value was `undefined` and `JSON.stringify` dropped the key). Root cause, confirmed empirically (`docker exec accelerator-backend node -e "..."` querying the real model): `StudentPointsEvent`'s Sequelize model declares `timestamps: true, underscored: true`, which renames the DB COLUMN to `created_at` but does NOT rename the JS instance property — that stays `createdAt`. `pointsService.ts`'s `getPointsSummary()` read `r.created_at` (always `undefined`) instead of `r.createdAt` — a pre-existing bug that predates every change shipped today, so the Schedule/icon/room-link work earlier was correctly built against a backend contract that had simply never worked for anyone, on any account, since this feature shipped 2026-07-08–07-12.
    While diagnosing, found the exact same root-cause pattern independently broke a SEPARATE, unrelated function in the same file: `sumPointsTodayByEventTypes()` (the running total a daily anti-cheat points cap — `progression/dailyCap` — clamps against) explicitly requested `attributes: ['points', 'created_at']` in its Sequelize query; empirically confirmed via the same in-container script that passing the literal (unrecognized) attribute name `'created_at'` doesn't even fall back to `createdAt` — Sequelize silently drops it, so every row came back with NO date at all, meaning `new Date(undefined)` → Invalid Date → the `centralDateKey(...) === todayKey` check could never match → the daily point cap has silently never clamped anything, for any student, since it shipped. Fixed both: `getPointsSummary()` now maps `created_at: r.createdAt`; `sumPointsTodayByEventTypes()` now requests `attributes: ['points', 'createdAt']` and reads `r.createdAt`.
    Fixed the test that let this ship in the first place: `pointsService.test.ts`'s `getPointsSummary` test mocked `StudentPointsEvent.findAll` to return objects with `created_at` set directly — which is NOT what a real Sequelize instance looks like, so the test exercised a fake shape that happened to make the buggy code pass. Rewrote the mock to use `createdAt` (matching real Sequelize behavior) and added an explicit assertion that `res.events[i].created_at` actually carries the real date through. Added net-new test coverage for `sumPointsTodayByEventTypes`, which had zero direct tests before (only mocked-away in its callers) — one case proving same-type/same-day events sum correctly while a different-day event is excluded, one for the empty-list short-circuit.
  - Why: Ali: "I don't see any points" (on the real Schedule calendar, after the icon/spacing work shipped and was visually confirmed working for events).
  - Verification: New/updated unit tests — `pointsService.test.ts`, 13/13 passing, re-confirmed after merging a concurrent `origin/main` (docs-only, clean) (`node ../node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --config jest.config.ts src/services/__tests__/pointsService.test.ts`). `tsc --noEmit` clean in backend `src/` (267 pre-existing node_modules-only zod/d3 errors, unrelated, confirmed via grep). PR #859, all 4 CI checks green, merged via admin bypass, Ali confirmed "yes" to deploy. On prod: `git pull origin main` fast-forwarded exactly the 3 expected files (`pointsService.ts`, its test, PROGRESS.md); `docker compose ... up -d --build backend` (full backend rebuild required — this is backend logic, not a frontend-only change); confirmed `accelerator-backend` freshly started and healthy post-boot-window. **Re-verified against Ali's real account, live**: minted a fresh diagnostic JWT for `ali@colaberry.com` (enrollment `342113a0-a006-4e4c-bdb7-e443fbed322f`) and called the real `GET /api/portal/points` through `https://enterprise.colaberry.ai` — every one of his 5 real events now carries its actual `created_at` timestamp (`2026-07-24T01:02–01:15Z` ×3, `2026-07-27T22:28Z`, `2026-07-30T22:02Z`), where before the fix the field was silently absent from every event. This is the exact data Schedule's per-day badge logic (shipped earlier today, PR #829) needs — Ali should now see star badges on July 24, 27, and 30 on his real calendar.
  - Notes: This bug has been live since 2026-07-08–07-12 (the points-per-day feature's original ship date, per SchedulePage.tsx's own git history) — it did not regress today, and none of today's frontend work introduced it; the frontend was always correctly written against the documented `PointsEvent.created_at` contract. The anti-cheat cap finding (`sumPointsTodayByEventTypes`) is a real, separate security-relevant bug (the daily per-category point cap has silently never applied) surfaced as a side effect of this diagnosis — flagging it plainly rather than fixing it quietly and burying the finding; worth Ali's awareness even though the fix is bundled in the same one-line-root-cause commit. Did not audit other Sequelize models for the same `timestamps:true + underscored:true` + manual `.created_at` read pattern beyond points — `competencyEngine.ts`'s `EvidenceRecord.created_at` usage looked structurally similar during this investigation but is a different subsystem (Architect Readiness), out of scope for today, and not confirmed broken — worth a dedicated check.
### PaySimple webhook signature verification was rejecting every real payment — high-severity fix, backfilled 3 real students (2026-07-30)
- [x] **Traced a student's stuck subscription (14 checkout attempts, real payment, never activated) to a systemic bug: the PaySimple webhook signature check was structurally broken and had been rejecting every real webhook call. Fixed, deployed, and backfilled the real payments left stranded by it.**
  - Date: 2026-07-30
  - Session: CC-20260729-w4t8
  - What changed: Ali forwarded a message from Quincy Ninying — after the checkout-popup fix let him complete payment, his account still showed free-tier ("I haven't been enrolled yet"). Investigated properly rather than assuming a one-off: his `Subscription` record showed **14 separate checkout attempts, every one still `status: 'pending'`**, despite a real, receipted $199 payment. Checked backend logs and found the smoking gun: `[Webhook] PaySimple signature verification failed` — PaySimple was calling our webhook every time and we were rejecting it every time.
    Root cause: `webhookRoutes.ts` parsed the PaySimple webhook body with `express.json()`, handing the controller an already-parsed JS object. `webhookController.ts` then tried to reconstruct the "raw body" for HMAC verification via `JSON.stringify(req.body)` — which can essentially never reproduce the exact bytes PaySimple originally signed (key order, whitespace, and number formatting can all differ from the source), so signature verification failed deterministically on every real call, not intermittently. The GitHub webhook route in the same file already does this correctly (`express.raw()`, verify against the raw buffer, parse JSON only after verification passes) — applied the identical, already-proven pattern to the PaySimple route. Both webhook-driven payment paths were affected: `activateByRef` (self-serve `Subscription` activation, `SUB-` refs) and `markEnrollmentPaid` (the original enrollment payment path, `CB-` refs).
    12 existing tests were unaffected (the fix is backward-compatible for a non-Buffer body, which is what those tests simulate). Added 3 new tests exercising the real Buffer-bodied path: signature verified against exact raw bytes (deliberately formatted with different whitespace than a re-serialized version, to prove the distinction is real), a subscription ref activating correctly from a real Buffer body, and an invalid signature over a real Buffer body still correctly rejecting. PR #853, all 4 CI checks green, merged, deployed, confirmed live via compiled-file grep.
    **Backfilled the real payments this bug had stranded.** Quincy's actual completed payment (per PaySimple's own record, not just his forwarded receipt) was made under a different PaySimple customer identity than any of his 14 checkout attempts (his wife's card, a new customer record) — matched by timing to his closest-in-time attempt and activated via `activateByRef` directly, the same tested function the webhook itself calls. Given this was clearly not a one-off, swept every enrollment with a pending `Subscription` row (28 people, 67 attempts total) two ways: exact `paysimple_customer_id` match (0 hits — confirming the "different identity" pattern is common, not Quincy-specific) and a broader name-based cross-check against all reconcilable PaySimple payments >= $199. Most hits traced back to students already reconciled earlier tonight through other paths (their real seat already paid, only a stray duplicate row still showing pending — expected, not a new problem). Found exactly 2 genuinely new, previously untouched real payments: **Martin Mungai** ($1,788 Annual, settled 2026-07-21) and **Franck Kafando** ($199 Monthly, posted 2026-07-28) — both activated the same way, matched to their closest-in-time checkout attempt.
  - Why: Ali: "Can you check on Quincy's access after making his payment."
  - Verification: PR #853 CI green, deployed, confirmed live (`Buffer.isBuffer` present in the compiled controller). All 3 backfilled accounts (Quincy, Martin, Franck) re-verified via the real login-query simulation: each now resolves to `type=standard, payment_status=paid`. `activateByRef` itself is the same idempotent, already-tested function the (now-fixed) webhook calls, so no new write path was introduced for the backfill.
  - Notes: **This is very likely the deeper root cause behind a meaningful share of tonight's earlier manual payment reconciliations** — not just the previously-understood "side-channel payments never carry our external_id" gap, but payments that DID go through the app's own checkout flow, with a correctly-generated external_id, that still never auto-activated because the webhook confirming them was rejected at the door the entire time this bug existed. Unknown exactly how long that was (not logged/dated in this pass). **The remaining ~25 people with pending Subscription rows and no matching real payment were left untouched** — read as genuine abandoned/incomplete checkouts (clicking a plan without finishing payment is normal e-commerce behavior, not evidence of a bug) rather than assumed to be further victims; if any of them reach out claiming they paid, that claim should now be checked directly against PaySimple as the source of truth, the same way Quincy's, Martin's, and Franck's were, not dismissed. **Not addressed:** whether the existing `paymentReconciliationService.ts` cron (built earlier tonight) should be extended to also cover the `Subscription` model, not just `Enrollment.payment_status` directly — deliberately out of scope for this pass since the webhook path is now fixed going forward, but worth a follow-up if unmatched-customer-identity payments turn out to recur.

### PaySimple checkout silently 400ing for every credit-holding student (item.name > 50 chars) + 2 duplicate-account point merges (2026-07-31)
- [x] **Root-caused Pamela Manyika's "Could not start checkout right now" to a real, previously-unknown bug affecting all 25 students with an unapplied Open House credit; fixed, deployed, and verified live. Also verified prod deploy integrity end-to-end after Ali flagged "looks like none of them are fixed," and found + fixed a second real bug: Britiana Akhile had a live (non-withdrawn) duplicate account under a different email splitting her points.**
  - Date: 2026-07-31
  - Session: CC-20260729-w4t8
  - What changed: Ali reported Pamela's checkout failing and, separately, that Britania's fixes "looked unfixed," asking directly whether tonight's deploys had actually reached production. Took that at face value and verified deploy integrity first rather than assuming it was fine: `git fetch` + `git merge-base --is-ancestor` on the prod checkout confirmed HEAD matched `origin/main` and contained both PR #789 (QR check-in) and PR #853 (webhook signature) commits; grepped the *running* container's compiled `webhookController.js` for `Buffer.isBuffer` (3 occurrences) and the *served* nginx bundle for `colaberryCheckout` (the popup-blocker fix) to confirm what was actually live, not just what git said should be live. Both fixes were genuinely deployed and running — the deploy pipeline itself was not the problem.
    Reproduced Pamela's checkout failure directly (called `subscriptionService.startCheckout` server-side against her real enrollment) and got the real underlying error the generic frontend message was hiding: `PaySimple API error 400: "The length of 'Item. Name' must be 50 characters or fewer. You entered 54 characters."`. Root cause: `subscriptionService.startCheckout()` builds a `cohortName` string like `"Monthly plan (−$50 credit)"` (26 chars) whenever a credit applies, which `paysimpleService.createPaymentLink()` prefixes with `"AI Leadership Accelerator - "` (28 chars) to build the PaySimple `item.name` — 54 combined, 4 over PaySimple's hard limit. Moved his 1 point event and both Subscription rows (including the real PaySimple-confirmed payment, `paysimple_payment_id: 154970724`) onto his real account, withdrew both duplicates (including a third, empty Explorer row). Verified live: login resolves to the real account, `/api/portal/points` returns `total: 703` (22 events).
    While checking Shekia Phillips's "still seeing Free version, I've logged out a couple times" report (Ali suspected browser cache), found her real cause: she had just completed a genuine $149 payment (PaySimple `Authorized`, order matching her forwarded receipt) that never activated, because **the webhook is failing again** — grepped logs since the last deploy and found **30 for 30 real PaySimple webhook calls rejected** with the identical-looking `[Webhook] PaySimple signature verification failed` message from last night's already-fixed bug. Manually activated her real payment via `activateByRef` (the same tested, idempotent function the webhook calls) to unblock her immediately, then investigated the regression itself rather than assuming last night's fix had failed to deploy (it hadn't — confirmed the raw-body/Buffer signature-verification code from PR #853 was still correctly compiled into the running container).
    Root cause, found by reproducing it directly against the live production endpoint: `express.raw({ type: 'application/json' })` only engages its raw-body capture when the request's `Content-Type` header exactly matches `application/json`. Sent a correctly-HMAC-signed test webhook via curl with no explicit `Content-Type` header (curl defaults to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` in that case) and reproduced the exact failure: the raw parser skipped, `req.body` fell through to Express's default empty object, and the controller's already-correct fallback (`JSON.stringify(req.body)`) serialized that to the literal string `"{}"` — which cannot match any real signature, producing a clean 400 rejection with the same log line as the original bug but a completely different cause. This strongly indicates PaySimple's real webhook sender does not reliably send an exact `application/json` Content-Type (the adjacent GitHub webhook route in the same file uses the identical narrow matcher and is not failing, since GitHub's sender is consistent about this header). Fixed by changing the PaySimple route's matcher to `type: () => true` — captures the raw body unconditionally regardless of what Content-Type (or none) actually arrives, the standard pattern for payment-processor webhooks specifically because processors vary on this. GitHub's route was deliberately left unchanged. PR #871, all 4 CI checks green, merged, backend rebuilt and redeployed.
    No supertest/integration-test harness exists in this repo to add an automated regression test for Express route-level body-parser wiring (this bug lives in middleware configuration, not controller logic, so the existing `webhookController.test.ts` unit tests — which call the controller directly with a pre-built Buffer — cannot exercise or guard this specific failure mode). Used live curl verification against the real production endpoint instead, both to reproduce the bug pre-fix and to confirm the fix post-deploy: re-ran the same adversarial Content-Type cases (missing, form-urlencoded, `text/plain`, and the normal `application/json` baseline) against the live endpoint after redeploy — all 4 now return 200, and zero signature-failure log lines appeared for any of them. Two temporary diagnostic patches applied directly to the running container's compiled JS during the investigation (logging received-vs-expected signature and full request headers, to capture a real PaySimple call if one arrived before I could reproduce it manually) were confirmed washed away by the clean rebuild — `grep -c` for both diagnostic markers returns 0 in the freshly-built container.

All 3 (Shekia, Shabana, Marcus) activated via `activateByRef` and verified: `standard/paid/portal_enabled/active/member` with the correct `amount_paid`.

Webhook fix — live curl reproduction pre-fix (400, `"{}"`-stringified body) and post-fix (200 across 4 Content-Type variants including the exact failure case), zero signature-failure log lines since redeploy, diagnostic patches confirmed absent from the rebuilt container. ### Class Kit pace clock: real Stop control + 3-hour hard auto-cap (2026-07-30)
- [x] **Fixed the Present-mode class clock having no way to stop (only a destructive full Reset) and no ceiling — a forgotten tab was seen at 186 minutes elapsed / "BEHIND 181 MIN".   - Date: 2026-07-30
  - Session: CC-20260730-h6q2
  - What changed: Dhee reported the Class Kit "Present" deck's pace clock (`kitDeckScript.ts`, the client-side pace tracker in `#kpace`) had no stop control and kept counting indefinitely, and asked for a hard 3-hour cap plus auto-off when everyone leaves class — screenshotted live at 186:25 elapsed / "BEHIND 181 MIN" on a Thursday Build Day session. Root cause: the single `#kstart` button only ever toggled between "Start class" (sets a `localStorage` timestamp) and a destructive "Reset" (a `confirm()`-gated full wipe) — there was no way to end a run without erasing it, and `updatePace()`'s `setInterval` had no upper bound on `Date.now() - start`.
    Reworked the pace tracker into a proper 3-state machine (`kitDeckScript.ts`): not-started → running ("Stop class") → stopped ("Reset"). Clicking Stop while running freezes the clock at the current elapsed time (no confirm — it's the normal end-of-class action) rather than erasing it; Reset from the stopped state still confirms before clearing back to zero. Added `autoStopIfNeeded()`, called on every 1s tick and every live-pulse poll: force-stops at exactly `MAX_CLASS_MS` (3h) regardless of instructor action, and — for sessions with live pulse polling enabled — force-stops once the checked-in count (`pulse.present`) returns to 0 after having been seen above 0 (`sawPresence` guard, so it can't fire before the room ever fills). Status pill shows "CLASS ENDED" (new `.ended` style, amber, in `kitDeckStyles.ts`) once stopped/capped, and the clock display freezes rather than continuing to climb.
    Added `kitDeckScript.test.ts`: since the deck script is plain browser JS embedded in a `<script>` tag (no jsdom in this repo's Jest config — `testEnvironment: 'node'`), the tests run the real `deckScript()` output in a Node `vm` sandbox with a minimal fake DOM/localStorage and a controllable `Date.now()`, exercising the actual shipped code rather than a reimplementation. 3 tests: 3-hour cap freezes the clock exactly at 180:00 and it doesn't resume counting afterward; Stop freezes elapsed time without wiping it; Reset only clears on confirm, not on decline. The "everyone left" live-pulse branch is not covered by this suite (would need a fetch/microtask harness disproportionate to the risk of that ~4-line branch) — reviewed by hand instead.

    **Incident, caused while wiring the cron entry**: intended to `crontab -l >> file` (append) before editing, but actually ran `crontab -l > file` (overwrite) followed by editing that file and reinstalling it -- except the capture step redirected to a path on the *remote* host while the subsequent edit and `scp` happened against a *local* file of the same name that never had the original content, so the file that got `scp`'d back and installed via `crontab <file>` contained only the one new line. This replaced root's entire personal crontab (`/var/spool/cron/crontabs/root`) with a single entry, silently dropping roughly 36 other real production jobs: Basecamp token refresh/health-check (`refreshBasecampTokenFromVault.sh`, `refreshCbSystemToken.sh`, `bcTokenHealthCheck.sh`), the reporting pipeline (`runReportingAuditAndSend.js` x2 schedules, `weeklyCohortReport.js`, `weeklyInternReport.js`, `sendFamilyCommandCenterDaily.js` x2), the CB AI Ops workers (`inbound-dispatcher.js`, `worker.js`, `backlog-enforcer.js`, `cb-watchdog.js`, `cb-quality-audit.js`, 4x `runCbAiTasks*` project runners), `govContractsTurnWatcher.js`, `vipInboxWatcher.js`, `unsubscribe-health-check.js`, `dailyInternNudges.js`, `dailyAliRetrospective.js`, `sendAliDecisionsOwedDigest.js`, `paysimpleMissedPaymentsReport.js`, `syncEventbriteOpenHouseLeads.js`, `schemaDriftCheck.sh`, the shipces `dailyScrum.js`, `docker system prune`, `winback-launch.sh`/`winback-daily-report.sh`, `task-prompt-worker.sh`, `ata-report-digest.sh`, the AI Pathway comm pipeline, plus Landjet's `agent_heartbeat.sh` and Opportunity Pulse's `backup.sh` (both other systems sharing this host, unaffected by the accelerator repo but affected by this crontab, since it's one shared `root` crontab across every system on the VPS).
    No local backup existed (`/var/spool/cron/crontabs/` only holds the live file, no `.bak`; no infra-as-code copy of the crontab in any repo). Recovered from ~26 days of retained syslog (`/var/log/syslog` through `syslog.4.gz`), which logs every cron invocation's exact command line and timestamp: extracted all unique `CRON ... CMD (...)` command strings (filtered out genuine system-level entries from `/etc/crontab`/`/etc/cron.d` -- certbot, e2scrub, debian-sa1, anacron triggers -- which were never touched by this mistake, since `crontab <file>` only replaces the invoking user's *personal* crontab), then for every real command computed the full set of distinct days-of-week/hours/minutes it was actually observed running at across the full retention window (not a truncated sample). Every low-frequency (daily/weekly) job resolved to one clean, unambiguous schedule. The handful of every-N-minutes worker/watcher jobs showed a dominant base interval (`*/2`, `*/3`, `*/5`, or `*/15`) with a small amount of jitter noise (an occasional 1-minute-late firing, most likely system load, not a real second schedule) -- verified each base interval by checking that literally every multiple of the interval appeared in the observed minute set before trusting it. One real ambiguity: two variants of the shipces `dailyScrum.js` command existed in the history (with vs. without a `deliverables.js` copy step); dated each occurrence and found the `deliverables.js` variant has been the exclusive one running since 2026-07-16, so restored that one only.
    Rebuilt as a single crontab file, diffed the reconstructed command strings against the original observed set (byte-for-byte, ignoring only the intentional 2 additions and 1 intentionally-excluded stale duplicate) to catch any transcription typo before installing, syntax-checked with `crontab -n`, then installed. Confirmed live: jobs stopped appearing in syslog for the ~10-minute gap between the wipe and the fix, then resumed firing on schedule immediately after reinstall.
  - Why: Ali: "Go ahead and create the plan to turn this into a reusable asset. Then execute... I want to wake up to it being in production." The incident was self-inflicted during that execution, not requested or caused by Ali.
  - Verification: `crontab -n` syntax check passed before install. Reconstructed command strings diffed against the original syslog-observed set with zero unexpected differences. `crontab -l` post-install shows all 38 entries (36 recovered + payment reconciliation sweep + the new duplicate-account sweep). Live-confirmed jobs resumed firing on their reconstructed schedule within the next scheduling window after reinstall (`worker.js`, `govContractsTurnWatcher.js`, `vipInboxWatcher.js`, `inbound-dispatcher.js`, `agent_heartbeat.sh` all observed firing again in syslog post-recovery).
  - Notes: **This reconstruction is high-confidence, not guaranteed-perfect** -- it is built from ~26 days of observed behavior, not from an actual backup of the lost file, so a job that was very recently added (within the last few days, not yet establishing a clear pattern) or a job scheduled less frequently than the ~26-day retention window (e.g., monthly) could be missing or reconstructed with a slightly off schedule; nothing in the observed command list looked monthly, but that is inference from absence, not confirmation. **Ali should spot-check `crontab -l` against his own knowledge of these jobs** when he wakes up, particularly anything he knows runs less than monthly. The root cause of the mistake itself: ran a capture-then-edit-then-reinstall sequence across two different machines (remote capture, local edit, remote reinstall) without re-verifying the file's actual content immediately before the destructive `crontab <file>` install step -- the fix going forward is to always `cat` the file being installed immediately before `crontab <file>`, on whichever host will actually run the command, rather than trusting an intermediate variable/path to have round-tripped correctly.

Root cause: `ensureRoomForSession()` was only ever wired into `acceleratorService.createSession()` (a one-off/admin session-create path) — the function that actually builds a cohort's real schedule, `sessionGenerationService.generateSessionsFromCohort()`, creates `LiveSession` rows directly via `LiveSession.create()` and never called it. ### Root cause of the night's duplicate-account defect found and fixed (PR #913) — stops new duplicates at the source (2026-07-31)
- [x] **Traced why duplicate Explorer accounts kept getting created (9 real students found and manually fixed overnight, 2 sweep tools built to clean them up) back to two real bugs in `enrollmentService.ts`/`subscriptionService.ts`, fixed both, and verified live against a real account from tonight's own incident list.**
  - Date: 2026-07-31
  - Session: CC-20260729-w4t8
  - What changed: Ali: "yes" (approving the root-cause investigation flagged as the highest-leverage remaining item after the two sweep tools). Every fix shipped tonight up to this point -- the manual merges, `duplicateAccountSweepService.ts`, its cross-cohort extension -- treated the symptom: find a duplicate, merge it, withdraw it. None asked why the duplicates kept appearing in the first place. Traced it to `createExplorerEnrollment()`, the function behind both the live Open House registration endpoint (`POST /api/v1/open-house/register`) and the batch Eventbrite sync (`syncOpenHouseExplorers`): its "already registered" check was `Enrollment.findOne({ where: { email, cohort_id: cohort.id } })` -- scoped to the Explorer cohort *itself*. A student who already had a real, paid seat in a different cohort was completely invisible to that query, so a repeat Open House RSVP (the live endpoint's own doc comment claims it's "idempotent on email: repeat calls return the existing account without duplicating," which was false for exactly this case) or a resynced Eventbrite attendee row created a brand-new duplicate Explorer account every single time -- despite the code's own comment insisting it handled "a real paid student." Fixed by querying every ACTIVE enrollment for the email across all cohorts and resolving the real one via `pickBestEnrollment` (the same ranking function the actual login flow uses), so a caller who already has a real seat is routed back to it, and a caller who already has a pre-existing duplicate (from before this fix shipped) still resolves to their real account rather than an arbitrary row. No circular import risk (`participantService.ts`, which owns `pickBestEnrollment`, does not import from `enrollmentService.ts`).
    Second, related gap found and closed in the same pass: `enrollmentService.ts` already has `retireRedundantExplorerAccounts()`, which withdraws a lingering Explorer duplicate the moment a student's payment confirms -- but it was only ever wired into the legacy `CB-` external-id payment path (`markEnrollmentPaid`). Nearly every one of tonight's actual incidents (Sonya, Shekia, Shabana, Marcus, and others) went through the newer self-serve `Subscription`/checkout path (`activateByRef`), which never called it -- meaning the one existing safety net silently didn't cover the payment path most students actually use today. Wired the same retirement call into `grantMembership()`, the single function `activateByRef` and `grantFreeAccess` already both funnel through by explicit design (its own doc comment: "the two callers can never drift apart") -- so both self-serve payment and comped/admin-granted access now get the same lingering-duplicate cleanup the legacy path always has, best-effort and non-blocking, matching the existing call's exact pattern.
    7 new/updated tests across both files: the actual root-cause regression (a real enrollment in a different cohort is reused, not duplicated -- modeled directly on Sonya Parker's real incident), picking the real account over a pre-existing duplicate when both are still active, updated idempotency coverage for the new `findAll`-based lookup, and 3 `subscriptionService` tests confirming the retirement call fires on both `activateByRef` and `grantFreeAccess` and never blocks activation if the retirement lookup itself errors. PR #913, all 4 CI checks green, merged, backend rebuilt and redeployed.
  - Why: Ali: "yes" (in direct response to: "Want me to start on #7 (the root cause)... this pattern has now hit 8 people in one night").
  - Verification: Live-verified against a real account from tonight's own incident list rather than only trusting unit tests -- called the deployed `createExplorerEnrollment('Sonya Parker', 'sonya28tx@gmail.com')` directly inside the running container (she has 2 enrollment rows on file: her withdrawn duplicate + her real active one). Result: `created: false`, correctly returned her real enrollment id, row count for her email stayed at 2 before and after -- no new duplicate created, reproducing the exact original bug scenario and confirming it no longer occurs. Compiled-container grep confirmed both `pickBestEnrollment` (enrollmentService.js) and `retireRedundantExplorerAccounts` (subscriptionService.js) present in the deployed build.
  - Notes: This closes the loop that started with Ali's "Mungai lost his points" message several entries ago -- the sweep tools built in #878/#908 remain valuable as an ongoing backstop for anyone already affected or any future edge case, but this fix is what actually stops the roster from acquiring new duplicates going forward. **Not verified in this pass**: whether `syncOpenHouseExplorers` (the batch Eventbrite path, as opposed to the live registration endpoint) has ever historically re-synced the same attendee more than once in a way that would have hit this exact bug -- the fix covers both call sites identically, so no separate action is needed there, but the historical blast radius wasn't specifically audited beyond the 9 students already found and fixed by hand or via the sweep tools.

Before deploying, verified the fix two ways beyond unit tests: (1) ran the real service via `ts-node` against the actual local registry file — 53%/13, matching pre-bug expectations; (2) built a standalone simulation of the exact Docker directory layout (a scratch `dist/services/` with `docs/ai-governance/` copied 2 levels up, junctioned to real `node_modules`) and ran the real (unmodified) service file from inside it — resolved correctly via the fallback candidate to the same 53%/13. All 4 CI checks green on PR #930 (`Backend typecheck`, `Backend unit tests`, `Frontend typecheck`, `Secret scan + route-auth lint`); admin-merged, pulled onto prod (fast-forward `0f5cae49..c9e3e36f`, picking up this PR plus the earlier doc-only PR #926 in one pull since prod hadn't been pulled since the very first Phase 1 deploy), rebuilt `backend` only (no frontend changes in this fix). Post-deploy, verified live in the running container rather than trusting the build's exit code alone: `docker exec accelerator-backend ls /app/docs/ai-governance/` now shows the CSV actually present; calling `getInpactGoalsEstimate()` directly inside the container returns the real `{"inpactEstimatePct":53,"goalsEstimate":13,"tier1SystemCount":10,"scoredSystemCount":10,...}` instead of zeroes.

Worth flagging as a pattern for future runtime-file-reading code: any service that reads a static file off disk at runtime (not `import`ed/bundled) needs to be verified against the actual Docker image layout, not just local `ts-node`, before being called "deployed" — the local dev environment structurally cannot catch this class of bug because `backend/dist` isn't flattened locally the way the image flattens it.

### Inbox Intel — Case Resolution Engine: live-testing bug fix + knowledge-base loop + Tickets board integration (2026-07-31)
- [x] **Fixed a real bug Ali hit live in production (case stuck in NEEDS_ALI after answering its last question, Close Case failing with no visible next step), plus two feature requests from the same live session: consult/grow a knowledge base so Ask doesn't re-ask documented answers, and surface all case work in the existing Tickets board.**
  - Date: 2026-07-31
  - Session: CC-20260731-x9q4
  - What changed: **(1) Bug fix** — `handleAnswerQuestion` never re-checked whether the answer just given was the LAST open blocking question, so a case sat in `NEEDS_ALI` forever after that point: no Plan step ever appeared, and Close Case failed with a checklist that gave no clue why nothing was progressing. Added `caseRepository.ts::maybeAdvanceFromNeedsAli()` (counts remaining `OPEN` questions, transitions `NEEDS_ALI -> READY_TO_PLAN` when zero remain) and wired it into `handleAnswerQuestion` right after every answer. **(2) Knowledge base loop** (Ali: "make sure it has the knowledgebase at its discretion... an iterative looping process that collects information, updates the knowledgebase"). Investigated the repo and found the intended target isn't a page (`/knowledge` doesn't exist — `/admin/knowledge-ops` does) but `CoraKbEntry`/`kbService.ts`, the operational Q&A store already used by Cora's live customer-facing auto-replies (`question_pattern`/`answer_template` with cohort-merge-tag resolution, `automation_potential`, `escalation_logic`) plus the marketing FAQ (`AdmissionsKnowledgeEntry`). New `services/inboxCase/caseKnowledgeService.ts`: read side (`buildKnowledgeReferenceBlock`) queries both KBs and feeds matches into the Phase 3 assessment prompt as a trusted `<<<KNOWLEDGE_BASE>>>` block — the system prompt now instructs the model to answer from an "auto-answerable" match as a confirmed fact instead of asking Ali, only needing approval to send; write side (`learnFromAnsweredQuestion`) proposes a NEW `CoraKbEntry` from every answered question, wired into `handleAnswerQuestion`. Deliberately **always `is_active: false`** — that table feeds Cora's live replies to real prospects, so an unreviewed AI-synthesized entry must never go live automatically; it lands in the exact review queue the existing `/admin/knowledge-ops` UI already shows (`GET /api/admin/kb/entries?active=false`), no new admin surface needed. Inbox Intel's own read path is the one exception: it also considers its own inactive-but-self-learned entries (tagged `main_category: 'Inbox Intel — Learned'`) so a case-resolution answer helps THIS system immediately without waiting on human review, while Cora's existing `queryKbForCora`/`buildCoraSystemPromptFromDB` (unchanged, still `activeOnly: true`) never see them until Ali activates one. Deduped by question-text/keyword-overlap so repeatedly answering "the same" question doesn't spam the review queue. **(3) Tickets board integration** (Ali: "All work should be done in a ticket by the agents... make it to where if it is working, then I can see the work being done in a ticket"). New `services/inboxCase/caseTicketService.ts`, wired centrally into `caseRepository.ts::openCase()`/`transitionCase()`/`reopenCase()` (the sole choke point for every case state change) rather than scattered per-service: every case gets one `Ticket` (deduped via `createTicket()`'s own `entity_type:'inbox_case'`/`entity_id`/`type` matching, reusing the existing `services/ticketService.ts` — the actively-validated path with real transition-state enforcement, not the parallel `ticketOrchestrator.ts`), walked through the board's real `backlog->todo->in_progress->in_review->done` state machine via a BFS path-walker (case states don't map 1:1 onto the board's mostly-linear columns) as the case progresses, with narrative progress-note comments at assessment/plan/execute/verify/close (mirrors the existing `platformFixAgent.ts` pattern). A reopened case whose prior ticket already reached `done` (terminal — no path back) gets a fresh ticket rather than trying to un-terminate the old one. Added a "View Ticket" deep-link (`/admin/tickets?open=<id>`, reusing the board's existing approval-email deep-link support) to the case workspace UI. Every ticket-sync call is best-effort (try/catch, logged, never throws) so a Tickets-board hiccup can never break the actual case workflow. Found and fixed 2 real bugs in the shared test-fake-model helper while testing this (not in the feature itself): `Object.entries()` silently ignores Symbol-keyed Sequelize `Op.or`/`Op.and` conditions, so the fake previously returned EVERY row instead of filtering on any such query; and `.count()` wasn't implemented at all. Both fixed in `testHelpers/fakeModel.ts`, benefiting all future tests in this suite. Also found and fixed a real tokenizer bug in the new KB service: filtering only `length > 2` let 3-letter stopwords like "the" through, meaning any query containing a common word would fuzzy-match nearly every KB entry — now reuses `textNormalization.ts`'s existing `STOPWORDS` set (newly exported for reuse).
  - Why: Ali, live in production: "I answered the question it gave me and then clicked Close Case and got this error... Has that process even been built? Make it to where if it is working, then I can see the work being done in a ticket. All work should be done in a ticket by the agents. What is the error asking me to do?" and, in the same session: "the knowledgebase should be updated as well... an iterative looping process."
  - Verification: `npx jest src/services/inboxCase` — 17 suites, **237/237 tests passing** (36 new: `caseKnowledgeService.test.ts` 15, `caseTicketService.test.ts` 14, `caseRepository.test.ts` 7 including 4 directly exercising the NEEDS_ALI fix). Backend `tsc --noEmit` clean except the same pre-existing unrelated `interviewService.ts` error. Frontend `tsc --noEmit` clean.
  - Notes: Not yet verified against the real production `CoraKbEntry`/`AdmissionsKnowledgeEntry` corpus (empty in this repo's fixtures — the read/write logic is unit-tested against synthetic entries, not confirmed to surface a real match for a real prospect question yet). Ali's specific stuck production case needs a one-time manual nudge post-deploy (its question was already answered before this fix shipped, so the fix's own trigger point already fired-and-missed for that one case) — covered as an explicit post-deploy verification step, not left as a dangling loose end.
