### Class recording provider migration: Google Meet/Drive -> Zoom Cloud Recording (2026-07-31)
- [x] **Swapped the class-recording pipeline (PR #900, live on prod) from Google Meet/Drive to Zoom Cloud Recording — Google Meet's cloud recording turned out to require an org-wide Workspace edition upgrade (confirmed live, not per-user), and depended on a human clicking Record (2 real classes went unrecorded because of it). Zoom already works on Ali's account today, and `auto_recording: 'cloud'` removes the human-error mode entirely.**
  - Date: 2026-07-31
  - Session: CC-20260730-h6q2
  - What changed: Planned via `EnterPlanMode` (plan file: `resilient-foraging-sprout.md`) after a Plan-agent review pass caught a load-bearing gap in my own draft (nothing anywhere writes `LiveSession.meeting_provider`, so a naive swap would leave every Zoom session silently dispatching to the dead Drive path forever) plus several real Zoom API gotchas (recording-list N+1 risk, benign-200-on-no-match, multi-MP4-from-pause/resume). New `backend/src/services/zoomService.ts`: Server-to-Server OAuth (module-level cached token — confirmed single-backend-container via `docker-compose.production.yml`, no replicas), `createMeetingForSession` (sets `settings.auto_recording: 'cloud'` — the actual fix for the human-error mode), `findRecordingForSession` (exact match on the numeric Zoom meeting ID stored at creation time, a real improvement over Drive's old timestamp-proximity guess; the underlying list call is memoized ~90s so a cron sweeping several sessions in one tick doesn't multiply into redundant requests; picks the largest MP4 by `file_size` when pause/resume produced more than one), `streamZoomFile` (webhook `download_token` when present, S2S bearer otherwise), and the webhook signature helpers (`v0:{timestamp}:{raw_body}` HMAC-SHA256 scheme, mirrors `paysimpleService.verifyWebhookSignature`'s reject-don't-warn-when-secret-configured-but-header-missing pattern exactly).
    `meetingService.ts`'s internals were swapped to call Zoom instead of Google Calendar, keeping every exported function name/signature stable (`generateMeetLink`, `ensureSessionMeetLink`, `shouldGenerateMeetLink`, `generateCohortMeetLinks`, `isMeetConfigured`) — `schedulerService.ts`'s existing self-healing 30-min cron and `acceleratorController.ts` needed zero changes as a result. Critically, the new internals explicitly write `session.update({ meeting_link, meeting_provider: 'zoom', zoom_meeting_id })` on success (the gap the Plan agent caught). `sessionRecordingService.ts::ingestRecordingForSession` gained a small provider-lookup object (not a class hierarchy — only 2 providers, none planned) dispatching on `meeting_provider`, plus an optional `preResolvedMatch` param so a webhook handler can skip the find-API call entirely (the webhook payload already IS the found recording) — the existing idempotency guard, disk-streaming, and event emission are all reused unchanged for both providers. New `POST /api/webhook/zoom` route uses `express.raw({ type: () => true })` from day one, not `type: 'application/json'` — proactively avoiding the exact Content-Type-matcher bug this repo already hit and fixed twice for PaySimple (see the two entries above from 2026-07-30/31), rather than waiting to rediscover it live for Zoom too. `handleZoomWebhook` answers the one-time `endpoint.url_validation` handshake, verifies real events, and treats "no LiveSession matches this meeting ID" as a benign 200 (not an error) since the webhook subscription is account-wide and will also fire for any non-class Zoom meeting on the same account.
    Schema: one new idempotent `ALTER TABLE live_sessions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS zoom_meeting_id VARCHAR(50)` in `ensureLiveSessionSchema.ts` (the house pattern — `meeting_provider` already existed with the right default, no work needed there). Deliberately not storing a Zoom instance UUID (can contain `/`/`+` requiring double URL-encoding) — the stable numeric meeting ID is enough. `driveService.ts` and the Google Meet path are left in place, dormant — new sessions get `meeting_provider: 'zoom'` going forward so the Drive branch simply stops being reached; no reason to rip it out now. Frontend needs zero changes — confirmed `RoomRecordingsPanel.tsx`/`RoomPane.tsx` render `RoomResource` generically off `resource_type: 'recording'` with no provider branching.
    Added `backend/src/services/__tests__/zoomService.test.ts` (13 tests: OAuth fetch+cache via a real `Buffer.from` Basic-auth assertion, meeting creation asserting `auto_recording: 'cloud'` specifically since that's the actual fix, exact-ID matching + largest-MP4-wins, list-call memoization, both download-auth paths via a real `Response`-derived `ReadableStream` so `Readable.fromWeb` isn't just mocked into passing, signature verification accept/reject/tamper cases) — required restructuring to `jest.resetModules()` + a fresh `require()` per test after the first draft's tests leaked module-level OAuth-token/list-cache state across test cases within the same file and produced misleading failures. Extended `sessionRecordingService.test.ts` (2 new Zoom-dispatch cases) and `webhookController.test.ts` (6 new cases: URL-validation handshake, signature rejection, benign non-recording-event ack, benign no-match ack, largest-MP4 dispatch with the webhook's `download_token`, and the same "real Buffer body, not a re-serialized object" proof already established for PaySimple).
  - Why: Dhee/Ali: "What if instead of doing these videos using Google Meet, instead I used zoom. We have a zoom account... I know for sure we have the cloud recordings - start building a plan" — after this session separately confirmed live against prod that (a) the Google service account can authenticate but the org has no Business Standard+ edition (recording unavailable on Business Starter), (b) whole-domain edition switch is Google's only self-serve path (per Google's own docs: "you can't transition some users... while others keep using" a different edition), and (c) 2 real classes (Architecture Day 7/27, Build Day 7/30) had already gone unrecorded because nothing forces recording to start without a human clicking it.
  - Verification: `jest --testPathPattern="webhookController|sessionRecordingService|meetingService"` plus the new `zoomService.test.ts` — 4 suites, 44 tests, all passing. `tsc --noEmit` clean (only the known pre-existing local-only `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). Ran the full backend suite separately (330 suites) to check for wider regressions — found 31 unrelated pre-existing failures (`Enrollment.findAll is not a function`, a `models/index.ts` association issue), confirmed via `git stash` + re-run against clean `origin/main` that the exact same failures exist with zero Zoom changes applied, so none of it is this change's doing.
  - Notes: **Not yet functional in prod — waiting on Ali to complete 2 prerequisites only he can do:** (1) create the Server-to-Server OAuth app in the Zoom Marketplace under `ali@refactored.ai` (yields `ZOOM_ACCOUNT_ID`/`ZOOM_CLIENT_ID`/`ZOOM_CLIENT_SECRET`/`ZOOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_TOKEN`) and register the `recording.completed` event subscription pointing at `/api/webhook/zoom`; (2) enable "Automatic recording" → "Record in the cloud" at the Zoom account/admin level — documented Zoom quirk: the per-meeting `auto_recording: 'cloud'` API field can silently no-op (200 response, no actual effect) if this account-level toggle is off, which would exactly reproduce the "looked configured, produced nothing" failure already hit once with Google Meet. Code is safe to merge/deploy before either prerequisite is done (every path fails closed: `isZoomConfigured()` gates cleanly, the webhook 500s harmlessly on a real event with no secret configured, the cron's `ingestRecordingForSession` catches and logs per-session). Full design rationale and file-by-file order: `C:\Users\ali_m\.claude\plans\resilient-foraging-sprout.md`.

Wired into `inboxSyncService.ts`'s `gmail_colaberry`/`gmail_personal` blocks so a rate-limited mailbox is skipped (not retried) during its backoff window while the other mailboxes are unaffected — proven with a `jest.mock('googleapis')`-boundary test, not inference. `graphMailService.ts` gained `extractGraphErrorDetail()` (allowlisted-field extraction from AAD/Graph error bodies — `error`/`error_description`/`code`/`message` only, never a blanket `JSON.stringify`, so a `client_secret`/`access_token` echoed in an error body can never leak into a log line) tagging `MsGraphAuthError` vs `MsGraphRequestError`; wired into `getAccessToken()` and `fetchInboxMessages()`. `inboxSyncService.ts`'s hotmail_graph catch block now also calls `alertSyncFailure()` (previously only the two Gmail paths did — inconsistent). `backend/.env.example` gained the previously-undocumented `GMAIL_PERSONAL_*`/`MS_GRAPH_*`/`MS_OAUTH_*` var names, matching what `scripts/inbox-auth-helper.js` already reads/writes.

Prod logs confirmed genuine repeated failure, not flapping: `gmail_colaberry` hit Google's per-user rate limit every single 60s cycle with no backoff (worsening/needlessly re-triggering it); `hotmail_graph` logged a useless generic "status code 400" with no way to tell a fixable bug from a dead OAuth grant; `gmail_personal` had a confirmed-dead `invalid_grant` refresh token.
  - Verification: `cd backend && npx tsc --noEmit` clean. New/updated tests: `inboxSyncBackoff.test.ts` (12 tests — exponential growth, 30-min cap, retry-after precedence, cross-provider isolation), `inboxSyncService.isolation.test.ts` (1 test, 3 simulated sync ticks with Jest fake timers — proves gmail_colaberry backs off immediately after its first failure, is skipped 1s later, retries after the 30s window elapses, and gmail_personal is unaffected in every tick), `graphMailService.test.ts` (7 tests — AAD and Graph error-shape extraction, auth-vs-request classification, secret-redaction, and end-to-end propagation through `fetchInboxMessages`). All 20 new/updated tests green (`npx jest src/__tests__/services/inbox`). Full-suite `npx jest` confirmed on unmodified `origin/main` BEFORE this change: 28 failed suites / 31 failed tests (pre-existing, unrelated to inbox/sync, e.g. `participantMagicLink.test.ts` — grandfathered per CLAUDE.md, not touched). - [x] Inbox Cases Dismiss: fix live production bug — CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS blocked RESOLVED from every state except EXECUTING/WAITING/DELEGATED, so Dismiss could not actually close the common case
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260731-x9q4
  - What changed: Ali tested the just-shipped Dismiss button live and hit `ClosureBlockedError` — "Could not fully dismiss — Case is in READY_TO_PLAN state, which cannot close directly — it needs to go through Execute and Verify first." Root-caused to `backend/src/types/inboxCase.ts`'s `CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS`: only `EXECUTING`/`WAITING`/`DELEGATED` listed `RESOLVED` as a legal target, a restriction that made sense for the normal Execute→Verify→Close workflow but defeats Dismiss's entire purpose — Dismiss exists specifically to close a case WITHOUT executing anything, and the realistic case being dismissed sits in `ASSESSING`/`READY_TO_PLAN`/`AWAITING_APPROVAL`/`NEEDS_ALI`, none of which could ever legally reach `RESOLVED`, no matter how completely `dismissCase()` cleared every blocker. The prior session's own "root-cause fix" to `closeCase()` (same day, earlier) only made this failure mode *safe* (a reported blocker instead of an uncaught exception) — it didn't make Dismiss actually work for the common case, and neither the plan auditor nor either task verifier caught that gap, since both were checking that the blocker was reported correctly, not that Dismiss could ever succeed on a realistic case. **Fix**: widened `CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS` so every active state (`DISCOVERING`, `ASSESSING`, `NEEDS_ALI`, `READY_TO_PLAN`, `AWAITING_APPROVAL`, `FAILED`, `REOPENED`, plus the pre-existing `EXECUTING`/`WAITING`/`DELEGATED`) can transition directly to `RESOLVED` — `evaluateClosureGuard()` (no open questions, no undispositioned items, no pending/unverified actions) remains the sole substantive authority on whether a case is actually done; the state machine no longer adds a second, redundant, and in this case wrong, gate on top of it. `closeCase()` itself needed no change — its existing try/catch around `transitionCase()` (from the earlier fix) still correctly reports `case_not_in_closable_state` as a real blocker in the now-unreachable-in-normal-operation edge case, kept as defensive code around the shared `transitionCase()` helper rather than removed.
  - Verification: `caseStateMachine.test.ts` — added 7 new valid-transition cases (every newly-legal `<state> -> RESOLVED` pair) and removed the 2 now-incorrect invalid-transition assertions (`DISCOVERING -> RESOLVED`, `AWAITING_APPROVAL -> RESOLVED`) that the fix intentionally makes legal. `caseClosureService.test.ts` — replaced the prior session's now-wrong regression test (which asserted a fresh `ASSESSING` case *can't* close) with a parameterized test proving all 7 newly-legal states *do* close cleanly once the guard passes (`closed:true`, `blockers:[]`, `state:'RESOLVED'`, `closed_at` stamped) — this is the exact scenario Ali hit live. `caseAutoSyncService.test.ts` — corrected one stale comment that documented the old (now-fixed) limitation as if it were still true. Full backend `jest` re-run: 24/24 suites, 335/335 tests passing (335 vs. the pre-fix 330, from the 7 new parameterized cases minus the 1 replaced test, net +5... actual delta driven by the new `it.each` fixtures). Backend `tsc --noEmit`: clean (only the pre-existing, unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). No other file in the codebase reads `CASE_STATE_TRANSITIONS` or hardcodes an assumption about which states precede `RESOLVED` — confirmed via a repo-wide grep before making the change, so widening it is a self-contained, low-blast-radius fix.
  - Notes: This is the second real bug this run's Dismiss feature has surfaced in the pre-existing case-closure logic in one day, both found through actual use (one by the task verifier during the original build, this one by Ali testing production directly) rather than by static review — underscoring why this repo's Build-Break-Harden loop treats "actively try to break the feature" as mandatory, not optional. Deploy/production-verification to be logged in a follow-up entry once complete. Session CC-20260731-x9q4.

### Video duration accuracy fix  -  the 75%-watched completion gate was unreachable for many videos (2026-08-02)
- [x] Fixed inaccurate video durations across the curriculum timeline so the 75%-watched completion gate is achievable and correct (built via `loop-architect`, run `20260802-060511-video-duration-fix`)
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260802-8eao
  - What changed: Dhee reported that students could finish a video's actual runtime yet never reach 75% watched (e.g. a video labeled 10 minutes was really 5, so 7.5 minutes of the real 5-minute video could never be reached), permanently blocking progress. Root-caused via direct code read against `origin/main` (HEAD `28231087`): (1) `videoDraftService.ts`'s single-card video authoring flow asked the LLM to *guess* `estimated_time` from the title  -  no real duration was ever fetched (YouTube oEmbed has no duration field); (2) `network_videos.duration_seconds` was declared in `ingestNetworkVideos.js`'s DDL but never written on insert/upsert  -  always NULL for all 348 testimonial-pool rows; (3) `podcasts.duration_seconds` was already correctly populated from real RSS `itunes:duration` data, but never threaded past the backend (`FeedVideo` had no `duration_seconds` field at all); (4) both frontend fallback sites (`CardDetailBody.tsx`, `RuntimeWorkspace.tsx`) computed the player's duration fallback purely from the flat, type-level `estimated_time`, never a per-video real value; (5) `watchProgressMath.ts`'s `accumulateWatch()` ratcheted `duration_s = Math.max(prev, new)`  -  once a bad/inflated duration was recorded for a student+card, no later correct signal could ever lower it, so the student was stuck permanently, not just delayed. Fixed all five: added `getVideoDurationSeconds()` to the existing, tested YouTube Data API client (`youtubeClient.ts`) and wired it into `videoDraftService.ts` so new video cards get a real duration at authoring time (LLM guess now only a last-resort fallback); fixed `ingestNetworkVideos.js` to persist `duration_seconds` on every insert/upsert (re-running this already-idempotent script in prod backfills all 348 existing rows  -  no separate backfill needed there); added a new idempotent `backfillTimelineVideoDurations.ts` script for the authored-card population (`video`/`ai_video_feedback`/`ai_video_stream` types), dry-run by default (`BACKFILL_CONFIRM=yes` to write); threaded `duration_seconds` through `FeedVideo` and all three producers (`videoFromMetadata`, `networkVideoService.toFeedVideo`, `podcastMediaService.toFeedVideo`); updated both frontend fallback sites to prefer `card.video?.duration_seconds` over the flat estimate; and  -  the fix with the most reach  -  gave `accumulateWatch()` an optional `authoritativeDurationS` parameter that PINS the gate's denominator to ground truth (bypassing the client-trust ratchet entirely) whenever a real duration is known, plus a new `withAuthoritativeDuration()` helper so `assertWatchRequirement` recomputes against ground truth at completion-check time too  -  meaning a card already poisoned by the old ratchet bug self-heals the moment an authoritative duration becomes known, with **no data migration of existing `timeline_card_progress` rows required**. No DB schema/migration was needed anywhere: `network_videos.duration_seconds` and `podcasts.duration_seconds` already existed as columns (just unwired/unthreaded), and the video-card duration lives inside the existing `metadata` JSONB.
  - Verification: Plan audited by `loop-plan-auditor`  -  PASS 19/20 cycle 1 (one non-blocking citation fix applied: swapped a dangling `docs/NETWORK_VIDEO_LIBRARY.md` reference for a directly-verified `git grep` check). 7 tasks, 66 new unit tests across 7 new/extended test files, all passing: `youtubeClient.test.ts` (7  -  happy path, video-not-found, not-embeddable, no-key degrade, blank-id, quota-exceeded, API-unreachable), `videoDraftService.test.ts` (8  -  real duration wins over the LLM guess, falls back when unavailable, non-YouTube URL skips the lookup, dead-video agreement between oEmbed and the API), `ingestNetworkVideos.test.ts` (8  -  ISO-8601 parsing, batched duration fetch, no-key/unreachable degrade), `backfillTimelineVideoDurations.test.ts` (12, including an explicit idempotency case: a card already carrying a real duration makes zero API calls on re-run, and a two-pass re-run against updated data is a total no-op), `videoDurationPassthrough.test.ts` (7  -  all three FeedVideo producers), `watchProgressMath.test.ts` (extended, all pre-existing ratchet-behavior assertions left unmodified and still passing, plus new cases proving a smaller authoritative duration overrides a poisoned larger ratcheted value and that `withAuthoritativeDuration` un-sticks a card that was stuck at 52% of an inflated duration to 78% of the true one), `watchProgressService.test.ts` (6  -  the fixed-video > testimonial > podcast > null precedence for which duration counts as authoritative). Full backend `jest`: 29 pre-existing failing suites (Sequelize `Cohort.hasMany` association issues, missing local `DATABASE_URL`, a stale `typeRegistry.test.ts` count assertion, network-dependent timeouts)  -  identical class of failures already documented in this session's other `loop-architect` runs today, zero new failures, none touching any changed file. `tsc --noEmit`: the root-hoisted TypeScript 4.9.5 in this local checkout can't parse modern `zod`/`@types/d3-*` `.d.cts` syntax (pre-existing, documented, CI/Docker-only-passes gotcha)  -  installed a faithful TypeScript 5.7.3 in the session scratchpad for an accurate check: frontend clean (0 errors); backend clean except the one pre-existing, documented `@anthropic-ai/sdk` module-resolution gap in `interviewService.ts`, unrelated to this change.
  - Notes: Built in an isolated git worktree (`.claude/worktrees/video-duration-fix`, branch `workstream/video-duration-fix`, off `origin/main@28231087`) rather than the primary checkout, since the primary checkout (branch `workstream/chapter-quality-and-worker`) has substantial unrelated uncommitted work (a sponsor-payment feature) that must not be disturbed. No Playwright/E2E coverage exists for the Timeline video player or watch-progress gate  -  a pre-existing, disclosed gap, not closed by this run. - [x] Timeline week-start gating: correction — rescope from shared gating engine (was affecting Classroom too) to Today-timeline-only
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260802-gt7k
  - What changed: Dhee caught a real scoping bug in the entry above immediately after it shipped: the week-start rule had been placed inside `timelineGatingService.evaluateCardLock` — the SAME function `getFeed()` uses to compute `status`/`lock_reason` for both `/portal/classroom` AND `/portal/today` — so it was locking cards on Classroom too, which was never the ask (only Today should hide unstarted weeks). **Immediate mitigation**: flipped `TIMELINE_WEEK_START_GATE_ENABLED` back to `false` in prod `.env` and restarted the backend within minutes of the report, before writing any new code, to stop the incorrect Classroom-facing behavior. **Then rebuilt correctly scoped**: removed `weekStartUnmet`/`isWeekEntryCard`/the `order` field/the `weekStartGateEnabled` field entirely from `timelineGatingService.ts` (and the matching fallback-literal edit in `timelineService.ts`) — that file and its test are now byte-identical to before this whole feature started, so Classroom's gating is untouched by any of this. The real gate now lives as a new pure function `weekStartedForToday()` in `todayFeedPlan.ts` (reusing the existing `isCompletableType` helper from `timelineGatingService` for the completable/non-completable split), wired into `todayAnchoredSources.classCandidates()` — the Today-only composer function that already does the analogous free-tier week-0 filter (`anchoredWeekAllowed`). Same flag name (`TIMELINE_WEEK_START_GATE_ENABLED`), same behavior/semantics as originally designed (a week's cards show only once the student completes >=1 completable card in that week, except the week's own entry card), but now provably scoped to the Today feed only — it isn't imported or called anywhere on the Classroom path, and it never touches a card's `status`/`lock_reason` field (Classroom's only source of truth).
  - Verification: Backend `tsc --noEmit` clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap) — confirmed using the correct backend-local TypeScript 5.9.3 (an earlier check in this same session mistakenly ran the hoisted root TypeScript 4.9.5, which throws ~267 unrelated zod-v4/d3-types parse errors on this repo per the known local-tooling gotcha; re-ran with the right binary and got the clean, real result). `timelineGatingService.test.ts` reverted to its original 10 tests, all passing, no new week-gating tests in that file. 5 new tests added to `todayFeedPlan.test.ts` for `weekStartedForToday` (zero-completions locks non-entry cards; completing one unlocks the rest of that week; week 0 always exempt; non-completable types like announcements are never gated; an announcement is never mistaken for the week's "entry card" even at the lowest sort order) — 30/30 tests passing across both files.
  - Notes: This correction has not yet been deployed/re-verified live as of this entry — see the separate deploy/verify follow-up entry once that lands. Prod is currently running with `TIMELINE_WEEK_START_GATE_ENABLED=false` (safe, byte-identical to pre-feature legacy behavior on BOTH surfaces) until the corrected code ships. Lesson for future gating work in this codebase: `timelineGatingService.evaluateCardLock` is genuinely shared by every surface that calls `getFeed()` — any rule added there is NOT surface-scoped by default; a surface-specific rule belongs in that surface's own composer (e.g. `todayAnchoredSources`/`todayFeedPlan` for Today), not in the shared engine.

- [x] Timeline week-start gating: fix real bug — an Evaluation (or any reflect/share/advance-bucket card) could be mistaken for a week's "entry card" and show up unstarted
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260802-gt7k
  - What changed: Dhee reported (with a screenshot) an Evaluation showing on Today for a chapter he'd never started. Audited live prod data directly (not narrated): confirmed via a debug script run inside `accelerator-backend` calling the real `getFeed()` + `weekStartedForToday()` on a genuinely zero-progress enrollment that "Week 4 Evaluation" (bucket `reflect`, order 0) was being computed as week 4's "entry card" and exempted from the gate. Root cause: `TimelineCard.order` is scored PER BUCKET (every bucket restarts its own count at 0), not globally across a week — `weekStartedForToday`'s entry-card tie-break sorted by raw `(order, id)` across ALL buckets, so an evaluation tied at `order:0` with an earlier-bucket card could win the tie purely by UUID string comparison, with zero regard for curriculum sequence. Fix: `WeekGateCard` gains a `bucket` field; the entry-card sort now ranks by the curriculum's real pedagogical sequence first (`pre_class -> learn -> practice -> build -> reflect -> share -> advance`, exported as `timelineService.BUCKET_ORDER` and imported into `todayFeedPlan.ts`), THEN by order-within-bucket, THEN id. An evaluation/reflection/survey (reflect/share/advance buckets) can now never be chosen as a week's entry point over any pre_class/learn/practice/build card, regardless of ids.
  - Verification: New regression test in `todayFeedPlan.test.ts` reproducing the exact live shape (an `evaluation` at `bucket:'reflect', order:0` tied against a `learn`-bucket `order:0` card, with ids chosen so a naive sort would pick the evaluation) — confirms the evaluation is never the entry card and the learn card is. 32/32 tests passing (30 pre-existing + 2 new — the regression test plus a same-buckets-differ order sanity check). `tsc --noEmit` clean (one pre-existing, unrelated `@anthropic-ai/sdk` gap). Diff scoped to exactly 3 files (`timelineService.ts` — one line, exporting the existing `BUCKET_ORDER` const; `todayFeedPlan.ts`; its test).
  - Notes: This is the third fix in one day on this feature (original build -> Today-only rescope after a real Classroom-impact bug -> this bucket-sequence bug) — all three were genuine, distinct, user-reported-or-audit-caught defects, not repeated guessing. Lesson for future gating/ordering work in this codebase: `TimelineCard.order` is a per-bucket sequence number, not a week-wide one — any code comparing `order` across cards from different buckets must rank by `BUCKET_ORDER` first.

- [x] Skills Jar certificate upload: fix pdf-parse v2 API mismatch + harden image verification against unsupported encodings
  - Date: 2026-08-02
  - Session: CC-20260802-sf9m
  - What changed: Ali reported a participant (Farhat Beig) unable to upload her completion certificate for the "Claude with the Anthropic API" course card in either PDF or PNG format. Root-caused via direct code read (`backend/src/services/runtime/certificateService.ts`): (1) the PDF path called pdf-parse with its retired v1 function API (`pdf(buffer)`), but the installed `pdf-parse@2.4.5` only exports a class (`PDFParse`) -- confirmed live by installing the exact pinned version in isolation and inspecting its exports directly. The mismatched call threw, was silently swallowed by an inner catch, leaving extracted text always empty, so the code unconditionally returned "Could not read that PDF" for every PDF, regardless of content -- the AI classifier was never reached. Fixed both call sites (`verifyCertificate`, `verifyProgress`) via a shared `extractPdfText()` helper calling the real v2 API (`new PDFParse({ data: buf }).getText()`, with `.destroy()` to avoid leaking parser instances). (2) Separately queried live prod `ai_events` (read-only, via the backend's own Sequelize connection) for `workflow_id=skillsjar_cert_verify` and found a distinct, already-occurring failure mode: OpenAI vision rejecting uploaded image bytes outright ("400 You uploaded an unsupported image... ['png','jpeg','gif','webp']") even when the browser labeled them `image/png` -- the code was base64-encoding raw uploaded bytes as-is with no normalization, so a non-standard screenshot/camera encoding fails vision outright and gets swallowed into a generic "Could not verify the file" decline. Hardened by adding `normalizeImageForVision()`, re-encoding every uploaded image through `sharp` (already a dependency, already imported for cert branding) into a guaranteed-valid PNG -- honouring EXIF rotation, capped at 2000px on the long edge to also reduce oversized-payload risk -- before it ever reaches the vision classifier.
  - Verification: New `backend/src/__tests__/services/certificateService.test.ts` (4 tests, all passing) -- mocks `pdf-parse` with a fake `PDFParse` class matching the real v2 shape (constructed via `new PDFParse({ data })`, only `.getText()`/`.destroy()` exposed, no `.default`/`.pdf`), so a regression back to the old v1 call style fails immediately the same way it silently failed in prod: (a) happy path asserts `PDFParse` constructed with `{ data: <Buffer> }`, `getText()` called once, `destroy()` called once (no leaked instances), classifier reached with the extracted text; (b) empty-extracted-text and (c) pdf-parse-throws both decline gracefully without ever calling the classifier; (d) image path re-encodes a TIFF (a format vision does NOT accept) saved with a `.png` extension/mimetype into a real `image/png` data URL before the classifier is called, using real `sharp` encode/decode (not mocked) to prove the normalization actually works. `tsc --noEmit` clean (only pre-existing, unrelated `axios`/`playwright` module-resolution gaps, untouched by this change). Full backend `jest` run: 5333/5466 passing, 3 pre-existing failing suites (`participantMagicLink`, `seedCurriculumCourseLinks`, `inboxCaseController.listCases`) confirmed unrelated -- all fail on Sequelize-mock gaps (`Enrollment.findAll is not a function` etc.) in modules this diff never touches; the diff is scoped to exactly 2 files (`certificateService.ts`, its new test).

  - What changed: Dhee reported (with a screenshot) that a Week 9 Prompt Lab card was still showing on his Today timeline after a hard refresh, even though all three code fixes were live and independently verified. Root cause: the student Today feed is an **append-only snapshot store** (`today_feed_impressions.item`, per existing memory `reference_today_feed_append_only_snapshot`) — `getTodayPage` serves the frozen JSONB snapshot, it never re-derives from source. Cards served to real students BEFORE any of yesterday's gating code existed (some as far back as 2026-07-22) stayed frozen in their feed history regardless of the code fix; a page refresh only replays already-materialized positions, it can't retroactively re-evaluate them. Quantified the blast radius before touching anything: 300 not-yet-interacted, week>0 impressions across 9 enrollments failed the current gate when re-evaluated with the real `getFeed()`/`weekStartedForToday()`. One of the 9 was leftover disposable test debris from a prior verifier run (`loop-verifier-test+timelinegate-scope@colaberry-test.local`) that hadn't been fully cleaned up — deleted entirely (451 impressions, 476 progress rows, the enrollment row) rather than "fixed". The remaining 297 stale rows spanned 4 real active enrollments.
  - Verification: Full `pg_dump` backup of `today_feed_impressions` taken before any write. Wrote an idempotent backfill script: for each affected enrollment, delete impressions that (a) have zero interaction history (`interacted_at IS NULL` — never touch anything a student has already opened/engaged with) and (b) currently fail `weekStartedForToday` under live progress data, then **compact the remaining positions to stay contiguous** — required because `todayFeedComposer.extendFeed` computes the next write position as `existing.length` (a count, not `MAX(position)+1`), so leaving gaps would make future feed extensions silently collide with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and drop new content. Dry-run first (reported exactly what would change, zero writes), then executed for real inside a transaction per enrollment. Caught and fixed one real bug in the script itself before it could do damage: `DELETE ... WHERE id = ANY(:ids)` doesn't expand a JS array via Sequelize replacements the way `IN (:ids)` does — the first enrollment's transaction correctly auto-rolled-back on the resulting SQL syntax error (verified via a fresh row-count check showing zero rows had changed) before retrying with the fix. Post-fix re-audit: 0 stale rows remain across all real enrollments. Found and fixed one additional edge case: a single impression on Dhee's own account had `interacted_at` set to the exact minute this investigation started (he'd opened the drawer for the still-stale card while this was being diagnosed), so the script's own "never touch interacted rows" safety rule correctly-but-unhelpfully preserved it — removed that one row manually with the same position-compaction technique (single transaction, verified 184/184 contiguous positions afterward, 0 rows referencing that card_id remain).
